articles.title: A fighter pilot had unexplained headaches for over a year. The cause was hiding in plain sight.
articles.author: Mindy Weisberger

paras.en: The symptoms: The man, a fighter pilot in the Indian Air Force, went to a civilian neurologist after having persistent headaches for 18 months. The headaches would occur approximately two to three times per month, starting in the late afternoon and lasting up to three days. Sleep did not improve his symptoms.
paras.zh: 症状：这名男子是印度空军的一名战斗机飞行员，在持续头痛 18 个月后去看了一位民间神经科医生。头痛每月大约发生两到三次，从下午晚些时候开始，持续长达三天。睡眠并没有改善他的症状。

paras.en: The pain was typically greater on the right side of his head, but he would often feel pain on the left side as well. The pilot also reported that just before a headache, he would experience a "sense of lousiness," his doctors wrote in a report of the case.
paras.zh: 他头部右侧的疼痛通常更严重，但他的左侧也经常感到疼痛。他的医生在一份病例报告中写道，这名飞行员还报告说，在头痛之前，他会感到一种“恶心的感觉”。

paras.en: Sometimes, the pain was so intense that the man was unable to take part in scheduled flights. If he flew anyway during an episode, his headache would be even worse the next day.
paras.zh: 有时，疼痛非常剧烈，以至于该男子无法参加定期航班。如果他在发作期间无论如何飞行，第二天他的头痛会更严重。

paras.en: What happened next: According to the man, his finances and personal relationships were not a source of stress. (Stress, in general, is a very common headache trigger.)
paras.zh: 接下来发生了什么：据该男子称，他的财务和个人关系并不是压力来源。 （一般来说，压力是一种非常常见的头痛诱因。）

paras.en: When asked about his medical history, the pilot recalled no recent ailments or conditions that could cause recurring headaches, such as inflammation and congestion of the sinuses (sinusitis). He had no family history of chronic headaches or migraine, a neurological disease that frequently causes moderate to severe headache, among other symptoms. Nor did he experience nausea, vomiting or visual anomalies called "auras," which often accompany or precede migraines.
paras.zh: 当被问及他的病史时，飞行员回忆起最近没有任何可能导致反复头痛的疾病或状况，例如鼻窦炎症和充血（鼻窦炎）。他没有慢性头痛或偏头痛的家族史，这是一种经常引起中度至重度头痛等症状的神经系统疾病。他也没有出现恶心、呕吐或称为“先兆”的视觉异常现象，这些现象通常伴随或先于偏头痛。

paras.en: Nevertheless, the civilian doctor determined that migraines were the culprit. He prescribed divalproex — an oral medication used for migraine prevention — and told the patient that he would likely need this medication for years. Concerned about taking the drug over a long period, the pilot decided to consult an authorized specialist at a military medical facility for further evaluation.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，平民医生还是确定偏头痛是罪魁祸首。他开了双丙戊酸（一种用于预防偏头痛的口服药物），并告诉患者他可能需要这种药物多年。由于担心长期服用该药物，飞行员决定咨询军事医疗机构的授权专家进行进一步评估。

paras.en: Get the world’s most fascinating discoveries delivered straight to your inbox.
paras.zh: 将世界上最迷人的发现直接发送到您的收件箱。

paras.en: The diagnosis: The military doctors reviewed the pilot's case and examined him. All of his test results were in the normal range, and a CT scan showed no brain abnormalities. They ordered a nasal endoscopy — an exam that uses a camera to examine the nasal cavity and sinuses — and found that the patient had a deviated septum. However, the deviation was so minor that they ruled it out as a possible cause of his pain.
paras.zh: 诊断：军医对飞行员的情况进行了检查并进行了检查。他的所有检查结果都在正常范围内，CT扫描显示大脑没有异常。他们要求进行鼻内窥镜检查——一种使用摄像头检查鼻腔和鼻窦的检查——结果发现患者的鼻中隔偏曲。然而，这种偏差非常小，以至于他们排除了这是造成他疼痛的可能原因。

paras.en: Finally, the doctors agreed with the initial diagnosis: The pilot was experiencing migraines. The causes of migraine are not fully understood, although genetics and environmental factors may contribute to both the duration and intensity of migraine pain in a given individual.
paras.zh: 最后，医生们同意了初步诊断：飞行员患有偏头痛。尽管遗传和环境因素可能会影响特定个体偏头痛的持续时间和强度，但偏头痛的原因尚不完全清楚。

paras.en: The treatment: The pilot was given the migraine medicine sumatriptan, to be taken at the first sign of pain, and aspirin, to be taken during headaches. He was allowed to continue flying under restricted conditions, and he had to report to a military neurologist for monthly reviews over the next three months.
paras.zh: 治疗：飞行员服用了偏头痛药物舒马普坦（在出现疼痛迹象时服用）和阿司匹林（在头痛时服用）。他被允许在受限条件下继续飞行，并且必须在接下来的三个月内向军事神经科医生报告每月接受检查。

paras.en: Four months later, he was headache-free and had stopped taking medication, according to the report. However, his superior officers needed a detailed medical review before they could restore his unrestricted flight status, as severe migraines can disqualify pilots from flying.
paras.zh: 据报道，四个月后，他的头痛消失了，并停止服药。然而，他的上级官员需要进行详细的医疗检查，然后才能恢复他的不受限制的飞行状态，因为严重的偏头痛可能会导致飞行员失去飞行资格。

paras.en: Over three days, doctors conducted in-depth interviews with the pilot, focusing on the first appearance of his symptoms and the circumstances leading up to his headaches. They were puzzled by certain details: His lack of nausea, vomiting and auras, and the fact that he got no relief through sleep. These facts raised questions about the migraine diagnosis.
paras.zh: 在三天的时间里，医生对飞行员进行了深入的采访，重点关注他最初出现的症状以及导致他头痛的情况。他们对某些细节感到困惑：他没有恶心、呕吐和光环，而且他无法通过睡眠得到缓解。这些事实引发了对偏头痛诊断的质疑。

paras.en: During the interviews, the pilot recalled that his headaches began around the time that he started using a new type of helmet with a tighter fit. The headaches corresponded with days in which he flew multiple flights and became worse the longer he wore the helmet. Then, around the time he started taking the prescribed medication, he coincidentally received a new allotment of personal flying clothing — including a helmet that was the correct size — for a new plane assignment. His headaches suddenly stopped.
paras.zh: 在采访中，飞行员回忆说，当他开始使用一种更紧的新型头盔时，他的头痛就开始了。头痛与他乘坐多次航班的日子相对应，戴头盔时间越长，头痛就越严重。然后，在他开始服用处方药的时候，他碰巧收到了一套新的个人飞行服装，包括尺寸合适的头盔，以适应新的飞机任务。他的头痛突然停止了。

paras.en: "At that point the officer did not connect the cessation of headaches with the use of the new helmet," the doctors reported. "Reviewing the case in its entirety, the diagnosis of migraine or vascular headache was found to be incorrect; instead the individual was suffering from external compression headache due to an ill fitting helmet."
paras.zh: 医生报告说：“当时，这名警官并没有将头痛的消失与使用新头盔联系起来。” "Reviewing the case in its entirety, the diagnosis of migraine or vascular headache was found to be incorrect; instead the individual was suffering from external compression headache due to an ill fitting helmet."

paras.en: Compression headaches are caused by tight external pressure on the scalp and forehead, and they typically resolve when the pressure eases.
paras.zh: 压迫性头痛是由头皮和前额受到过大的外部压力引起的，通常在压力缓解后就会消失。

paras.en: Doctors instructed the pilot to keep a headache diary and scheduled follow-up visits to confirm their findings. Five months later, his headaches had not returned, as he'd continued using the better-fitting helmet.
paras.zh: 医生指示飞行员记下头痛日记，并安排随访以确认他们的发现。五个月后，他的头痛没有再出现，因为他继续使用更合适的头盔。

paras.en: What makes the case unique: When the military doctors scoured peer-reviewed studies, they found no reports of similar instances of compression headache "in any of the Air Forces of the world," they wrote in the report.
paras.zh: 这个案例的独特之处在于：当军医们仔细研究同行评审的研究时，他们在报告中写道，“世界上任何一支空军”都没有发现类似的压迫性头痛病例的报告。

paras.en: This case, they added, emphasizes the medical significance of making sure that pilots' flight uniforms — especially their helmets — fit properly.
paras.zh: 他们补充说，这个案例强调了确保飞行员的飞行制服（尤其是头盔）正确合身的医学意义。

paras.en: For more intriguing medical cases, check out our Diagnostic Dilemma archives.
paras.zh: 如需更多有趣的医疗案例，请查看我们的诊断困境档案。

paras.en: This article is for informational purposes only and is not meant to offer medical advice.
paras.zh: 本文仅供参考，并不旨在提供医疗建议。

paras.zh: Kharbanda, P.、Ganjoo, R.K. 和 Chadha, D.S. (2008)。战斗机机组人员头痛的奇怪案例：案例研究。印度航空航天医学杂志，52(1)，20-25。 https://indjaerospacemed.com/a-strange-case-of-headache-in-a-fighter-aircrew-a-case-study/

paras.en: Mindy Weisberger is a science journalist and author of "Rise of the Zombie Bugs: The Surprising Science of Parasitic Mind-Control" (Hopkins Press). She formerly edited for Scholastic and was a channel editor and senior writer for Live Science. She has reported on general science, covering climate change, paleontology, biology and space. Mindy studied film at Columbia University; prior to LS, she produced, wrote and directed media for the American Museum of Natural History in NYC. Her videos about dinosaurs, astrophysics, biodiversity and evolution appear in museums and science centers worldwide, earning awards such as the CINE Golden Eagle and the Communicator Award of Excellence. Her writing has also appeared in Scientific American, The Washington Post, How It Works Magazine and CNN.
paras.zh: 明迪·韦斯伯格（Mindy Weisberger）是一名科学记者，也是《僵尸虫的崛起：寄生精神控制的令人惊奇的科学》（霍普金斯出版社）的作者。她曾担任 Scholastic 的编辑，也是 Live Science 的频道编辑和高级作家。她报道了普通科学，涵盖气候变化、古生物学、生物学和太空。明迪在哥伦比亚大学学习电影；在加入 LS 之前，她为纽约美国自然历史博物馆制作、撰写和指导媒体。她有关恐龙、天体物理学、生物多样性和进化的视频出现在世界各地的博物馆和科学中心，赢得了电影金鹰奖和杰出传播者奖等奖项。她的文章还发表在《科学美国人》、《华盛顿邮报》、《How It Works》杂志和 CNN 上。

articles.title: Extremely rare Viking Age coin from the reign of 'Olaf the Holy' may have been 'held in the king's own hand'
articles.author: Tom Metcalfe

paras.en: A rare silver coin minted during the reign of a famous Viking king has been discovered in a massive hoard in Norway that now comprises 5,500 coins and counting.
paras.zh: 在挪威的一个巨大宝库中发现了一枚著名维京国王统治时期铸造的稀有银币，目前该宝库包含 5,500 枚硬币，并且还在不断增加。

paras.en: The coin is inscribed with the name of the Norwegian king Olaf Haraldsson, who ruled from 1015 to 1028 and, as St. Olaf or "Olaf the Holy," is considered the national saint of Norway.
paras.zh: 硬币上刻有挪威国王奥拉夫·哈拉尔松 (Olaf Haraldsson) 的名字，他于 1015 年至 1028 年在位，被称为“圣奥拉夫”或“圣奥拉夫”，被视为挪威的国家圣人。

paras.en: Fewer than 20 coins minted during Olaf's reign have ever been discovered, and the newfound coin is a "national treasure," according to a statement from the University of Oslo's Museum of Cultural History.
paras.zh: 奥斯陆大学文化历史博物馆的一份声明称，奥拉夫统治时期铸造的硬币不到 20 枚，新发现的硬币是“国宝”。

paras.en: "Here we have a coin bearing the king's portrait and a cross, with another cross on the reverse," University of Oslo coin expert Svein Gullbekk said in the statement. "It is a Christianisation coin on a grand scale."
paras.zh: 奥斯陆大学硬币专家斯文·古尔贝克在声明中说：“这里有一枚硬币，上面有国王的肖像和一个十字架，背面还有另一个十字架。” “这是一枚规模宏大的基督教化硬币。”

paras.en: Olaf is credited with establishing Christianity in Norway — an early step toward its full conversion about a generation later.
paras.zh: 奥拉夫被认为在挪威建立了基督教——这是大约一代人后彻底皈依基督教的早期步骤。

paras.en: "We can see how King Olaf used coinage to legitimise the new faith and to establish himself as a Christian king of European standing," Gullbekk said. "This is branding."
paras.zh: 古尔贝克说：“我们可以看到奥拉夫国王如何利用铸币使新信仰合法化，并确立自己作为欧洲基督教国王的地位。” “这就是品牌。”

paras.en: Haraldsson learned about Christianity when he joined Viking raids against England and France as a young man, and he was baptized in the French city of Rouen in about 1013, according to the statement.
paras.zh: 声明称，哈拉尔森年轻时参加维京人对英格兰和法国的袭击时了解了基督教，并于 1013 年左右在法国城市鲁昂接受了洗礼。

paras.en: Get the world’s most fascinating discoveries delivered straight to your inbox.
paras.zh: 将世界上最迷人的发现直接发送到您的收件箱。

paras.en: He became Norway's king in 1015, and in about 1024 proclaimed that only Christianity would be legal, according to the University of Bergen. Much of Norway, however, remained faithful to the Norse gods during his rule, especially around the central Trøndelag region and in the eastern parts of the country.
paras.zh: 据卑尔根大学称，他于 1015 年成为挪威国王，并于 1024 年左右宣布只有基督教才是合法的。然而，在他统治期间，挪威的大部分地区仍然忠于北欧诸神，特别是特伦德拉格中部地区和该国东部地区。

paras.en: But Olaf was made a Christian saint shortly after his death in 1030. He is now recognized as one of the first Christian kings of Norway and the first Norwegian king to issue coins in his own name.
paras.zh: 但奥拉夫于 1030 年去世后不久就被封为基督教圣人。他现在被认为是挪威最早的基督教国王之一，也是第一位以自己的名字发行硬币的挪威国王。

paras.en: The newfound coin is part of the Mørstad Hoard, which was discovered near the village of Rena in April. At that time, the buried hoard was described as the largest ever found in Norway and was estimated to contain almost 3,000 silver coins. However, subsequent research has determined that it includes anywhere from 5,500 to more than 6,000 coins, the statement said.
paras.zh: 这枚新发现的硬币是莫斯塔德宝藏的一部分，于四月在雷纳村附近发现。当时，埋藏的宝藏被描述为挪威有史以来发现的最大的宝藏，估计包含近 3,000 枚银币。然而，声明称，随后的研究确定其中包含 5,500 至 6,000 多枚硬币。

paras.en: Anne Skogsfjord, a museum researcher charged with cataloging the coins, thought the Olaf coin was an Anglo-Saxon penny at first. But then she read the inscription and realized it was minted in Norway under Olaf.
paras.zh: 负责对硬币进行编目的博物馆研究员安妮·斯科格斯菲尤尔 (Anne Skogsfjord) 起初认为奥拉夫硬币是盎格鲁撒克逊便士。但后来她读到了铭文，意识到它是奥拉夫在挪威铸造的。

paras.en: "I could see that it read ONLAF R+ NORMANORV. … Could this really be a coin of Olaf Haraldsson that I was holding?" Skogsfjord said in the statement. "And it was! It was a very special moment."
paras.zh: “我可以看到上面写着 ONLAF R+ NORMANORV。……这真的是我手里拿着的奥拉夫·哈拉尔森的硬币吗？”斯科格斯峡湾在声明中表示。 “确实如此！那是一个非常特别的时刻。”

paras.en: The coin was struck between about 1024 and 1028, near the end of the Viking Age, and circulated for 20 to 25 years before someone deposited it in the hoard, the statement said.
paras.zh: 声明称，这枚硬币大约于 1024 年至 1028 年铸造，接近维京时代末期，在有人将其存入宝库之前流通了 20 至 25 年。

paras.en: - Dirty 'button' unearthed by metal detectorist turns out to be a rare 900-year-old coin from Norway's last Viking king, Magnus Barefoot
paras.zh: - 金属探测器发现的肮脏“纽扣”原来是挪威最后一位维京国王马格努斯·赤足 (Magnus Barefoot) 的罕见 900 年前硬币

paras.en: - 'Biggest surprise of my life': Homeowner discovers Denmark's largest Viking Age silver hoard in their backyard
paras.zh: - “我一生中最大的惊喜”：房主在自家后院发现了丹麦最大的维京时代银窖

paras.en: - 'There was something bigger in the ground here': Metal detectorist in Germany discovers giant Roman-era hoard from time of emperor Hadrian
paras.zh: -“这里的地下有更大的东西”：德国金属探测器发现了哈德良皇帝时期罗马时代的巨型宝藏

paras.en: Although the minting of the coin was a political and religious act, the coin also seems to have been used as currency; both sides bear numerous small cut marks, which was a common way of determining whether a coin was made completely of silver.
Gullbekk said Haraldsson himself had decided what the coins would look like and may have been present when they were minted.
paras.zh: 古尔贝克表示，哈拉尔森本人已经决定了这些硬币的外观，并且可能在铸造时就已经存在了。

paras.en: "It is entirely possible that this very coin from Mørstad was once held in the king's own hand," he said in the statement.
paras.zh: 他在声明中说：“这枚来自莫斯塔德的硬币完全有可能曾经握在国王本人手中。”

paras.en: See how much you know about ancient norsemen with our Viking quiz!
paras.zh: 通过我们的维京测验，看看您对古代北欧人了解多少！

paras.en: Tom Metcalfe is a freelance journalist and regular Live Science contributor who is based in London in the United Kingdom. Tom writes mainly about science, space, archaeology, the Earth and the oceans. He has also written for the BBC, NBC News, National Geographic, Scientific American, Air & Space, and many others.
paras.zh: 汤姆·梅特卡夫 (Tom Metcalfe) 是一名自由撰稿人，也是《Live Science》的定期撰稿人，常驻英国伦敦。汤姆主要撰写有关科学、太空、考古学、地球和海洋的文章。他还为 BBC、NBC 新闻、国家地理、科学美国人、航空航天等多家媒体撰稿。

articles.title: James Webb telescope discovers surprising trove of metals around the Milky Way's supermassive black hole
articles.author: Elizabeth Howell

paras.en: The Milky Way's supermassive black hole is surrounded by a surprising trove of heavy metals, according to new observations by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). The metals may offer new clues about how Earth got its share of heavy elements — but it could also make one of the greatest mysteries about our local black hole even harder to solve.
paras.zh: 根据詹姆斯·韦伯太空望远镜 (JWST) 的最新观测，银河系的超大质量黑洞周围环绕着大量令人惊讶的重金属。这些金属可能会提供关于地球如何获得重元素的新线索，但它也可能使我们当地黑洞的最大谜团之一变得更加难以解开。

paras.en: In astronomy, metals refer to any element heavier than hydrogen or helium, with common examples including oxygen, carbon, iron or gold. These elements are forged through nuclear fusion in the hearts of stars that are reaching the ends of their lives, before being sprayed into space and incorporated into new generations of stars.
paras.zh: 在天文学中，金属是指任何比氢或氦重的元素，常见的例子包括氧、碳、铁或金。这些元素是在生命即将结束的恒星中心通过核聚变形成的，然后被喷射到太空并融入新一代恒星中。

paras.en: Scientists say the material spotted by JWST likely came from supernovas — stellar explosions that blasted the metal into the region around Sagittarius A (Sgr A*), the monster black hole in the middle of our galaxy.
paras.zh: 科学家表示，JWST 发现的物质很可能来自超新星——恒星爆炸将金属喷射到人马座 A (Sgr A*) 周围的区域，人马座 A 是我们银河系中部的巨型黑洞。

paras.en: The metals, detected as gas, appear to have the same composition as several nearby stars, which suggests both the stars and the gas originated at the same time. Researchers shared the observations in a paper published Oct. 19 in The Astronomical Journal, following up on work published in The Astrophysical Journal in May.
paras.zh: 这些金属被检测为气体，似乎与附近的几颗恒星具有相同的成分，这表明恒星和气体是同时起源的。研究人员在 10 月 19 日在《天文学杂志》上发表的一篇论文中分享了这些观察结果，这是继 5 月份在《天体物理学杂志》上发表的研究成果的后续研究。

paras.en: "We know there's a black hole at the centre of our galaxy pulling material into itself, but we see that it's eating a lot less material than other supermassive black holes, and more slowly," Nicole Ford, first author of the new paper and a doctoral student in astrophysics at McGill University in Montreal, said in a statement. "Part of understanding why this is happening means looking at the properties of the materials available for it to consume, including gas, dust and the stars orbiting around it."
paras.zh: 这篇新论文的第一作者、蒙特利尔麦吉尔大学天体物理学博士生妮可·福特在一份声明中表示：“我们知道银河系中心有一个黑洞正在将物质拉入自身，但我们发现它吞噬的物质比其他超大质量黑洞要少得多，而且速度也更慢。” “要理解为什么会发生这种情况，就需要研究可供它消耗的材料的特性，包括气体、尘埃和围绕它运行的恒星。”

paras.en: JWST orbits at Lagrange point 2, which is about 1 million miles (1.5 million kilometers) from Earth in the opposite direction of the sun. The telescope identified the heat signatures of specific gas clouds billowing near the black hole, as well as the metal content within those clouds.
paras.zh: JWST 的轨道位于拉格朗日点 2，该点距离地球约 100 万英里（150 万公里），与太阳的方向相反。该望远镜识别了黑洞附近翻滚的特定气体云的热特征，以及这些云中的金属含量。

paras.en: "These findings could advance understanding of how metals are distributed around supermassive black holes in more distant galaxies, as well as the processes that supplied Earth with many of these elements," McGill researchers said in the statement. The metals' presence "influences how quickly gases cool, which in turn influences how readily the gas can be drawn into a black hole," they added.
paras.zh: 麦吉尔研究人员在声明中表示：“这些发现可以促进人们对更遥远星系中超大质量黑洞周围金属如何分布的理解，以及向地球提供许多这些元素的过程。”他们补充说，这些金属的存在“影响气体冷却的速度，进而影响气体被吸入黑洞的容易程度”。

paras.en: Get the world’s most fascinating discoveries delivered straight to your inbox.
paras.zh: 将世界上最迷人的发现直接发送到您的收件箱。

paras.en: The previous study in The Astrophysical Journal showed that gas emissions near the black hole have been influenced by conditions in the local clouds. Unfortunately, this means the gas alone cannot serve as a proxy for how often the black hole has been active, the researchers said.
paras.zh: 《天体物理学杂志》之前的研究表明，黑洞附近的气体排放受到当地云层条件的影响。不幸的是，研究人员表示，这意味着气体本身无法代表黑洞活跃的频率。

paras.en: Ford, N. M., Balakrishnan, M., Von Fellenberg, S. D., Haggard, D., Michail, J. M., Cui, Y., Hora, J. L., Neilsen, J., Principe, G., Roychowdhury, T., Sabha, N. B., Smith, H. A., Sumners, Z., & Willner, S. P. (2026). Ionization Structure and Metal Enrichment of the Galactic Center Minispiral Observed with JWST. The Astronomical Journal, 172(5), 267. https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/ae994d

P. （2026）。 JWST 观测到的银河系中心微型螺旋的电离结构和金属富集。 《天文学杂志》，172(5), 267。https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/ae994d

paras.zh: 通过我们的黑洞测验看看您对黑洞了解多少！

paras.en: Elizabeth Howell was staff reporter at Space.com between 2022 and 2024 and a regular contributor to Live Science and Space.com between 2012 and 2022. Elizabeth's reporting includes multiple exclusives with the White House, speaking several times with the International Space Station, witnessing five human spaceflight launches on two continents, flying parabolic, working inside a spacesuit, and participating in a simulated Mars mission. Her latest book, "Why Am I Taller?" (ECW Press, 2022) is co-written with astronaut Dave Williams.
paras.zh: 伊丽莎白·豪厄尔 (Elizabeth Howell) 于 2022 年至 2024 年间担任 Space.com 的特约记者，并于 2012 年至 2022 年间为 Live Science 和 Space.com 定期撰稿。伊丽莎白的报道包括白宫的多项独家报道、与国际空间站的多次对话、见证了在两大洲的五次载人航天发射、抛物线飞行、在宇航服内工作以及参与模拟火星任务。她的最新书《为什么我更高？》 （ECW Press，2022 年）与宇航员戴夫·威廉姆斯 (Dave Williams) 共同撰写。

articles.title: Shanghai's 'Audacious' New Opera House Just Opened Its Doors—and a Gravity-Defying Staircase—to the Public

paras.en: The world’s newest opera house officially opened its doors this week, featuring a bold architectural flair and a soaring spiral staircase that connects city streets to a rooftop stage and observation deck.
paras.zh: 世界上最新的歌剧院于本周正式开业，其建筑风格大胆，高耸的螺旋楼梯将城市街道与屋顶舞台和观景台连接起来。

paras.en: The Shanghai Grand Opera House now stands complete on the banks of China’s Huangpu River, a decade after Snøhetta, an architecture firm from Norway, won the international competition to design it.
paras.zh: 距离挪威 Snøhetta 建筑公司赢得国际设计竞赛十年后，上海大歌剧院现已在中国黄浦江畔落成。

paras.en: The nearly 1.6 million square-foot building is home to three separate auditoriums with a combined capacity of 4,200 seats. Its stages were built to accommodate myriad performances and rehearsals, from traditional operas to classical symphonies and experimental productions.
paras.zh: 这座近 160 万平方英尺的建筑拥有三个独立的礼堂，总共可容纳 4,200 个座位。它的舞台是为了容纳从传统歌剧到古典交响乐和实验作品的无数表演和排练而建造的。

paras.en: In a statement, Snøhetta describes the primary performance space—the 2,000-seat Harmony Hall—as a “finely tuned instrument, combining state-of-the-art theatre systems with carefully calibrated acoustics.” It contains five levels of seating and is furnished in dark reds.
paras.zh: Snøhetta 在一份声明中将主要表演空间（拥有 2,000 个座位的和谐厅）描述为“精心调校的乐器，将最先进的剧院系统与精心校准的音响效果相结合”。它有五层座位，并以深红色装饰。

paras.en: With 1,200 seats, the Soar Theatre was designed with baroque and classical opera in mind. The slightly smaller Open Stage, which offers panoramic views of the riverfront, prioritizes flexibility, with changing stage and seating configurations that can accommodate a variety of experimental performances. The main hall of the building is a stark white space, filled with natural light and sharp red accents.
paras.zh: 翱翔剧院拥有 1,200 个座位，其设计考虑了巴洛克和古典歌剧。稍小的开放舞台可以欣赏河滨全景，优先考虑灵活性，舞台和座位配置不断变化，可以容纳各种实验表演。建筑的主厅是一个纯白色的空间，充满自然光和鲜明的红色调。

paras.en: “A cultural building, any building for that matter, must respond to its surroundings, the people who use it, the performers it serves, and the city it becomes part of,” Kjetil Thorsen, the co-founder of Snøhetta, tells Dezeen’s Lizzie Crook. “When I last visited the site, I was asked by a Chinese architecture student how we managed to create a building that felt so Chinese despite not being from China. The answer lies in observation and understanding context.”
paras.zh: Snøhetta 的联合创始人 Kjetil Thorsen 告诉 Dezeen 的 Lizzie Crook：“一座文化建筑，任何建筑，都必须对其周围环境、使用它的人、它所服务的表演者以及它所属的城市做出回应。” “当我上次访问该网站时，一位中国建筑系学生问我，我们如何设法建造一座感觉如此中国的建筑，尽管它不是来自中国。答案在于观察和理解背景。”

paras.en: Visitors do not need a ticket to enter to the building or to explore its architectural flourishes. That philosophy of openness is embodied by the opera house’s massive exterior staircase, which rises from Shanghai’s riverfront, spiraling upwards to form the roof. It is meant to connect the the city’s existing walkways with an open-air observation deck, gathering spaces and a stage.
paras.zh: 游客无需门票即可进入该建筑或探索其建筑瑰宝。这种开放的哲学体现在歌剧院巨大的外部楼梯上，楼梯从上海的河边升起，螺旋上升形成屋顶。它的目的是将城市现有的人行道与露天观景台、聚会空间和舞台连接起来。

paras.en: “Buildings like opera houses inevitably create thresholds through walls, doors and ticketed programs,” Thorsen tells Dezeen. “We see it as our responsibility to challenge those thresholds and make the building as much a civic destination as a performance venue.”
paras.zh: “像歌剧院这样的建筑不可避免地会通过墙壁、门和售票节目设置门槛，”托森告诉 Dezeen。 “我们认为挑战这些门槛是我们的责任，使这座建筑既是一个表演场所，又是一个公民目的地。”

paras.en: Even on its own, the staircase is something to behold, akin to a large public sculpture. Its design is reminiscent of a traditional Chinese fan, a swirling dance movement, piano keys and the flow of the Huangpu River.
paras.zh: 即使楼梯本身也很引人注目，就像一个大型公共雕塑。其设计让人想起中国传统的扇子、旋转的舞蹈动作、钢琴键和黄浦江的流动。

paras.en: “The audacious architectural gesture now needs to be filled in with contents, with projects, with life, with people,” Serge Dorny, the director general of Germany’s Bavaria State Opera, tells ShanghaiEye.
paras.zh: 德国巴伐利亚国家歌剧院院长谢尔盖·多尔尼 (Serge Dorny) 告诉《上海之眼》：“大胆的建筑姿态现在需要充满内容、项目、生活和人。”

paras.en: The opera house’s inaugural season runs from October through February 2027. It will feature 82 performances, including ballet numbers from Russia’s Eifman Ballet and the American Ballet Theatre; a Beethoven cycle from Staatskapelle Berlin, one of the world’s leading orchestras; and traditional Chinese operas, called xiqu, including The Peony Pavilion and Dream of the Red Chamber.
paras.zh: 该歌剧院的首演季从 10 月持续到 2027 年 2 月。将有 82 场演出，包括俄罗斯艾夫曼芭蕾舞团和美国芭蕾舞剧院的芭蕾舞剧目；柏林国家管弦乐团（世界领先的管弦乐团之一）的贝多芬套曲；以及中国传统戏曲，称为戏曲，包括《牡丹亭》和《红楼梦》。

paras.en: Snøhetta has designed several opera house projects in recent years that combine performance with public accessibility. In Oslo, the waterfront Norwegian National Opera and Ballet opened in 2008. The firm’s design for the Busan Opera House in South Korea, another waterfront institution, is set to make its debut sometime in 2027, while the Royal Diriyah Opera House in Saudi Arabia is expected to open its doors in 2028.
paras.zh: Snøhetta 近年来设计了多个歌剧院项目，将表演与公共可达性结合起来。在奥斯陆，位于海滨的挪威国家歌剧院和芭蕾舞团于 2008 年开业。该公司为另一个海滨机构韩国釜山歌剧院的设计预计将于 2027 年首次亮相，而沙特阿拉伯皇家迪里耶歌剧院预计将于 2028 年开业。

paras.en: In recent years, Shanghai, a financial hub home to roughly 25 million people, has made a major push to establish itself as a cultural center. Since 2021, the Museum of Art Pudong, Shanghai Museum East, West Bund Grand Theatre and Shanghai Literature Museum have all opened their doors.
paras.zh: 近年来，拥有约 2500 万人口的金融中心上海大力推动文化中心建设。 2021年以来，浦东美术馆、上海博物馆东馆、西岸大剧院、上海文学馆相继开馆。

paras.en: “Accessibility is about daring to go in,” Thorsen tells CNN’s Stephy Chung. “It’s not only about the glass walls and the doors, but it’s about being attracted to the space as you come in, and you feel that even if you’re not the average opera goer, you’re invited in.”
paras.zh: “无障碍就是敢于进去，”托森告诉 CNN 的斯蒂芬·钟 (Stephy Chung)。 “这不仅仅是关于玻璃墙和门，而是当你进来时被这个空间所吸引，你会觉得即使你不是普通的歌剧观众，你也会被邀请进去。”

articles.title: African Elephants Shape the Savanna Ecosystem—and Continue Doing So Long After They've Died, Study Suggests

paras.en: African savanna elephants are considered ecosystem engineers. For up to roughly 70 years, each massive animal rips through trees and brush, digs wells in the ground and spreads seeds in its poop.
paras.zh: 非洲草原象被认为是生态系统工程师。在长达大约 70 年的时间里，每只大型动物都会撕扯树木和灌木丛，在地上挖井，并在粪便中传播种子。

paras.en: But even after their lives have ended, the hulking pachyderms continue making contributions to the environment, according to a study published October 12 in the journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. Scientists found a surprising chronology of events—involving microbes, plants and animals—near elephant remains that persists for at least eight years. The work highlights a relatively new line of research into how mega-carcasses affect the land.
paras.zh: 但根据 10 月 12 日发表在《美国国家科学院院刊》杂志上的一项研究，即使它们的生命结束了，这些巨大的厚皮动物仍然继续为环境做出贡献。科学家们在大象遗骸附近发现了令人惊讶的事件年表——涉及微生物、植物和动物——并且持续了至少八年。这项工作突出了关于巨型动物尸体如何影响土地的相对较新的研究方向。

paras.en: “We are really only fairly recently starting to get a handle on how large animals shape their ecosystems altogether, even in life,” Amanda Subalusky, an ecologist at the University of Florida who did not participate in the study, tells the Washington Post’s Meghan Bartels. “We are just beginning to scratch the surface on the role that their carcasses play.”
paras.zh: 佛罗里达大学的生态学家阿曼达·苏巴鲁斯基（Amanda Subalusky）没有参与这项研究，他告诉《华盛顿邮报》的梅根·巴特尔斯（Meghan Bartels）：“我们实际上只是最近才开始了解大型动物如何整体塑造它们的生态系统，甚至在生命中也是如此。” “我们才刚刚开始了解它们尸体所扮演的角色。”

paras.en: When an elephant named Alexander at Kruger National Park in South Africa died in 2009, study co-author Dave Thompson, a biodiversity scientist at the South African Environmental Observation Network, and a colleague started wondering how the carcass might affect the soil and food web, according to a statement.
paras.zh: 一份声明称，当南非克鲁格国家公园一头名叫亚历山大的大象于 2009 年死亡时，该研究的合著者、南非环境观测网络的生物多样性科学家戴夫·汤普森 (Dave Thompson) 和一位同事开始想知道大象尸体可能如何影响土壤和食物网。

paras.en: That curiosity turned into a larger effort to investigate soil chemistry, microbiology, biodiversity and herbivores feeding near 40 elephant carcasses in the park between 2023 and 2025. The animals had died between eight days and almost eight years before sample collection.
paras.zh: 这种好奇心转化为更大的努力，调查 2023 年至 2025 年间公园内近 40 具大象尸体的土壤化学、微生物学、生物多样性和食草动物。这些动物在采集样本前的八天到近八年之间就已死亡。

paras.en: Analyses revealed that initially, the large animal’s body kills off all biomass directly beneath it. Scavengers also swoop in to feast on the carcass, clearing the surrounding area. The remains leak nutrients into the ground, drastically boosting their levels. “At really fresh carcass sites, soil nitrogen concentrations can be up to 3,000 times higher” than locations without a carcass, says lead author Courtney Reed, an ecologist at Princeton University, in the statement. “That’s just insane.”
paras.zh: 分析显示，最初，这种大型动物的身体会杀死其正下方的所有生物量。食腐动物也会猛扑过来吃掉尸体，清理了周围的区域。遗骸将营养物质泄漏到地下，大大提高了它们的水平。主要作者、普林斯顿大学生态学家考特尼·里德在声明中表示，“在真正有新鲜尸体的地方，土壤氮浓度可能比没有尸体的地方高出 3000 倍”。 “这太疯狂了。”

paras.en: The flood of nutrients isn’t a good thing for plants. The sheer amount is toxic and stops their growth. On the other hand, microbial activity in the soil increases, though only in a small number of species.
paras.zh: 营养物质的泛滥对植物来说并不是一件好事。大量的有毒物质会阻止它们的生长。另一方面，土壤中的微生物活性增加，尽管只是少数物种。

paras.en: Once the nutrient concentrations eventually go down, plants behave similarly to the microbes, with just some fast-growing species taking over the hyperlocal environment for at least around eight years. These greens are particularly nutritious and attract grazing animals, which keep coming back to the site and fertilizing the land with their poop.
paras.zh: 一旦营养浓度最终下降，植物的行为与微生物类似，只有一些快速生长的物种占据超本地环境至少八年左右。这些绿色植物特别有营养，能吸引食草动物，它们会不断地回到这里，用粪便给土地施肥。

paras.en: “You have herbivores like zebra and buffalo and rhinos who are all coming in, and they’re selectively chewing on these nitrogen-rich grasses,” says Reed, who conducted the research while at the University of California, Santa Barbara, to Dave Seglins on the CBC’s “As It Happens.” “So, you actually get this burst of herbivore activity that continues for years after the elephants died.”
paras.zh: “像斑马、水牛和犀牛这样的食草动物都会进来，它们会选择性地咀嚼这些富含氮的草，”在加州大学圣塔芭芭拉分校进行这项研究的里德在 CBC 节目《As It Happens》中向戴夫·塞格林斯 (Dave Seglins) 说道。 “所以，你实际上看到了这种食草动物活动的爆发，这种活动在大象死后持续了数年。”

paras.en: There are two species of African elephants. Savanna elephants are larger and have outward-curving tusks, while forest elephants are darker and have straighter, downward-pointing tusks.
paras.zh: 非洲象有两种。稀树草原象体型较大，象牙向外弯曲，而森林象颜色较深，象牙较直、向下。

paras.en: The phenomenon somewhat resembles what happens when a whale dies. Its body sinks to the bottom of the ocean—a process called whale fall—and can fuel a jump in biodiversity and activity from all the organisms it attracts. It provides a plethora of nutrients in the deep ocean, where they’re scarce. But an elephant body delivers such a high concentration of nutrients in a fertile location that it instead causes a years-long biodiversity cold spot for microbes and vegetation.
paras.zh: 这种现象有点类似于鲸鱼死亡时发生的情况。它的身体沉入海底（这一过程称为鲸落），可以促进其吸引的所有生物体的生物多样性和活动的跃升。它在深海中提供了大量的营养物质，而这些物质在深海中是稀缺的。但大象的身体在肥沃的地方提供了如此高浓度的营养物质，反而给微生物和植被造成了长达数年的生物多样性冷点。

paras.en: Interestingly, the savannas might be especially prone to a strong, long-lasting ecological cascade. A mega-carcass might have a weaker impact in a more dynamic ecosystem, like a forest or wetland with lots of rain, or in a desert where droughts limit microbial and plant activity. The team hopes to test these ideas in sub-Saharan Africa, and they’ll continue monitoring the carcass sites in Kruger National Park to see how the land keeps changing.
paras.zh: 有趣的是，稀树草原可能特别容易产生强烈、持久的生态级联。在更具活力的生态系统中，例如多雨的森林或湿地，或者干旱限制微生物和植物活动的沙漠中，巨型尸体的影响可能较弱。该团队希望在撒哈拉以南非洲测试这些想法，他们将继续监测克鲁格国家公园的尸体地点，以了解土地如何不断变化。

paras.en: “There are hidden processes occurring underground all across our landscapes,” says Philip Barton, an ecologist at Deakin University in Australia, who wasn’t involved in the study, to the Washington Post. “And they are critical to driving ecosystem structure and function.”
paras.zh: 澳大利亚迪肯大学的生态学家菲利普·巴顿（未参与这项研究）对《华盛顿邮报》表示：“在我们的地貌中，地下都存在着隐藏的过程。”他没有参与这项研究。 “它们对于推动生态系统结构和功能至关重要。”

articles.title: Archaeologists May Have Solved the Mystery of a Roman Sarcophagus Excavated at Westminster Abbey in 1869

paras.en: When Arthur Penrhyn Stanley, the dean of Westminster Abbey, returned home after an 1869 trip to Italy, he was surprised to learn that in his absence, workers at the centuries-old London church had stumbled upon a limestone sarcophagus “belonging to the same epoch and nation as the great city which I had just quitted.”
paras.zh: 1869 年，当威斯敏斯特教堂院长阿瑟·彭林·斯坦利 (Arthur Penrhyn Stanley) 结束意大利之行返回家乡时，他惊讶地发现，在他不在的情况下，这座有着数百年历史的伦敦教堂的工作人员偶然发现了一个石灰石石棺，“与我刚刚离开的这座伟大城市属于同一时代和国家”。

paras.en: The find presented a mystifying puzzle: How did a seemingly ancient coffin end up in a medieval abbey? And whose body was buried inside it?
paras.zh: 这一发现提出了一个神秘的谜题：一把看似古老的棺材如何最终出现在中世纪的修道院里？而里面埋着的又是谁的尸体呢？

paras.en: Stanley detailed his study of the sarcophagus in an 1870 journal article. Although the coffin bore a Latin inscription apparently dated to the Roman occupation of Britain, its lid featured a large cross that was more consistent with the early medieval period, hundreds of years later. As the dean wrote, “There was nothing to indicate the rank of the person, nor in fact anything but the skeleton, with the exception of a few fragments of brick, apparently Roman brick, and a piece of dark gray, slag-like substance.” Still, Stanley concluded that the skeleton itself likely wasn’t Roman, instead dating to a later era.
paras.zh: 斯坦利在 1870 年的一篇期刊文章中详细介绍了他对石棺的研究。尽管棺材上的拉丁铭文显然可以追溯到罗马占领英国的时期，但它的盖子上有一个大十字架，这与数百年后的中世纪早期更加一致。正如院长所写，“除了几块砖块（显然是罗马砖块）和一块深灰色的矿渣状物质外，没有任何东西可以表明这个人的等级，事实上除了骨架之外什么也没有。”尽管如此，斯坦利得出的结论是，这具骨架本身很可能不是罗马的，而是可以追溯到更晚的时代。

paras.en: In the century and a half since the coffin was first excavated, scholars have offered varying explanations for its presence in the abbey, where only a few other Roman artifacts have been found. Now, archaeologist and architectural historian Warwick Rodwell has seemingly solved the mystery, drawing on radiocarbon dating and a skeletal analysis conducted by colleague James Langthorne to identify the sarcophagus’ occupant.
paras.zh: 自首次挖掘棺材以来的一个半世纪里，学者们对其在修道院中的存在提出了不同的解释，而修道院只发现了一些其他罗马文物。现在，考古学家兼建筑历史学家沃里克·罗德威尔（Warwick Rodwell）似乎已经解开了这个谜团，他利用放射性碳测年法和同事詹姆斯·兰索恩（James Langthorne）进行的骨骼分析来识别石棺的主人。

paras.en: In a paper published in the Journal of the British Archaeological Association, Rodwell argues that the skeleton likely belongs to Aelfwig, a monk who served as Westminster’s abbot (equivalent to a dean) prior to his death around 1020. Another possible candidate is Aelfwig’s successor, Wulfnoth.
paras.zh: 罗德威尔在《英国考古协会杂志》上发表的一篇论文中认为，这具骨架很可能属于艾尔夫维格，他是一位僧侣，在 1020 年左右去世前曾担任威斯敏斯特修道院院长（相当于院长）。另一个可能的候选人是艾尔夫维格的继任者武尔夫诺斯。

paras.en: “We have two viable contenders for the occupant of the sarcophagus,” Rodwell says in a statement. “We do not know the date of birth of either. But either would fit equally well if we assume the abbot was in his early 20s when the appointment was made and close to 50 when he died.” (Langthorne’s assessment identified the skeleton as a roughly 5-foot-9, 35- to 49-year-old man, contradicting earlier analyses that suggested he was slightly shorter and no older than 30.)
paras.zh: 罗德威尔在一份声明中说：“对于石棺的主人，我们有两个可行的竞争者。” “我们不知道他们的出生日期。但如果我们假设任命时方丈20岁出头，去世时接近50岁，那么任何一个都同样合适。” （兰索恩的评估确定这具骨架是一名身高约 5 英尺 9 英寸、年龄在 35 至 49 岁之间的男性，这与之前的分析相矛盾，之前的分析表明他略矮，年龄不超过 30 岁。）

paras.en: Stanley and his contemporaries looked to an inscription on the coffin for insights regarding its original owner. Translated into English, the message reads, “To the memory of Valerius Amandinus. Valerius Superventor and [Valerius] Marcellus made [this] for [their] father.”
paras.zh: 斯坦利和他的同时代人通过棺材上的铭文来了解其原主人。这条信息被翻译成英文，写道：“为了纪念瓦莱里乌斯·阿曼迪努斯。瓦莱里乌斯·超级文托和[瓦莱里乌斯]马塞勒斯为[他们的]父亲制作了[这个]。”

paras.en: Based in part on this eulogy, Victorian scholars dated the sarcophagus to between the second and fifth centuries. Rodwell, for his part, agrees with a theory put forth by Martin Henig, an archaeologist at the University of Oxford. As Rodwell notes in the paper, Henig argued that the coffin “was a Christian burial, probably of the Constantinian era,” in the early fourth century. Although the inscription’s “high quality” implies that Amandinus was “a significant figure in Roman London … nothing is known about his career,” Rodwell adds.
paras.zh: 部分基于这篇悼词，维多利亚时代的学者将石棺的年代定为二至五世纪之间。罗德威尔则同意牛津大学考古学家马丁·海尼格提出的理论。正如罗德威尔在论文中指出的那样，海尼格认为这口棺材是四世纪初的“基督教墓葬，可能是君士坦丁时代的”。罗德威尔补充道，尽管铭文的“高品质”意味着阿曼迪努斯是“罗马伦敦的一位重要人物……但我们对他的职业生涯一无所知”。

paras.en: Did you know? Famous faces at Westminster Abbey
paras.zh: 你可知道？威斯敏斯特教堂的名人面孔

paras.en: Notable individuals buried at Westminster Abbey include the Tudor monarchs Elizabeth I and Mary I, English polymath Isaac Newton, naturalist Charles Darwin, and poet Robert Barrett Browning.
paras.zh: 埋葬在威斯敏斯特教堂的名人包括都铎王朝君主伊丽莎白一世和玛丽一世、英国博学者艾萨克·牛顿、博物学家查尔斯·达尔文和诗人罗伯特·巴雷特·勃朗宁。

paras.en: As for the coffin’s Roman origins, Rodwell notes that ancient sarcophagi were sometimes reused centuries after their initial interment. The English monk Bede, for instance, wrote that the body of the seventh-century saint Elethdreda was buried in a “white marble coffin, most beautifully wrought,” that was found “near the city walls” of Grantacaestir, a Roman town near Cambridge, and brought back to the monastery where she’d served as abbess.
paras.zh: 至于棺材的罗马起源，罗德威尔指出，古代石棺有时会在最初埋葬几个世纪后被重复使用。例如，英国僧侣贝德写道，七世纪圣人埃勒斯德雷达的遗体被埋葬在“制作精美的白色大理石棺材”中，该棺材是在剑桥附近的罗马小镇格兰塔卡埃斯特“城墙附近”发现的，并被带回她曾担任女修道院院长的修道院。

paras.en: Rodwell tells the Guardian’s Nicola Davis that Westminster “was not [the coffin’s] original place of burial.” Instead, he suggests that the sarcophagus was taken from the wall recess of a mausoleum located elsewhere—a theory that would account for the absence of decorations on all but one of its sides. “Almost certainly, it was housed in a recess in a wall, so that only the inscribed front and the lid were visible,” the archaeologist writes in the study.
paras.zh: 罗德威尔告诉《卫报》的尼古拉·戴维斯，威斯敏斯特“不是[棺材]最初的埋葬地。”相反，他认为石棺是从位于其他地方的一座陵墓的墙壁凹进处取出的——这一理论可以解释除了一侧之外的所有侧面都没有装饰的原因。这位考古学家在研究中写道：“几乎可以肯定，它被安置在墙壁的凹槽中，因此只能看到刻有铭文的正面和盖子。”

paras.en: Exactly what happened to Amandinus’ skeleton, as well as how his coffin was selected to hold the abbot’s body, remains unclear. But radiocarbon testing of the skeleton that ultimately replaced Amandinus’ dated it to between 987 and 1052, offering a clearer sense of when the sarcophagus was repurposed.
paras.zh: 阿曼迪努斯的骨骼究竟发生了什么，以及如何选择他的棺材来容纳方丈的尸体，目前仍不清楚。但对最终取代阿曼迪努斯骨骼的放射性碳测试表明，该骨骼的年代是在 987 年至 1052 年之间，这让人们更清楚地了解石棺何时被改变用途。

paras.en: Around this time, the Roman-era lid was recut to feature a relief carving of a long cross, which distinguished it “as an important Christian burial,” Rodwell writes. The coffin was then buried beneath the floor of Westminster Abbey, where it likely remained until the mid-13th century, when the English king Henry III rebuilt the historic church in the Gothic style. Medieval builders moved the remains to the abbey’s sacristy, an L-shaped structure used to house sacred vessels and vestments.
paras.zh: 大约在这个时候，罗马时代的盖子被重新切割，上面刻有一个长十字架的浮雕，这使它成为“一个重要的基督教墓葬”，罗德威尔写道。随后棺材被埋在威斯敏斯特教堂的地板下，很可能一直保留到13世纪中叶，当时英国国王亨利三世以哥特式风格重建了这座历史悠久的教堂。中世纪的建筑者将遗骸移至修道院的圣器收藏室，这是一个 L 形结构，用于存放神圣的器皿和法衣。

paras.en: Workers removed the sarcophagus from the ruins of the demolished sacristy’s courtyard in 1869—but they weren’t the first to uncover the medieval burial. An oft-overlooked pencil sketch indicates that workers “wantonly broke” the coffin’s lid in 1820, removing the slab in search of treasures buried alongside the deceased. “The disarray recorded when the sarcophagus was next opened in 1869 is typical of looting, but we will never know whether any metal or other intrinsically significant objects were present and pilfered,” Rodwell explains in the paper.
paras.zh: 1869 年，工人们从被拆除的圣器收藏室庭院的废墟中移出了石棺，但他们并不是第一个发现这座中世纪墓葬的人。一幅经常被忽视的铅笔草图显示，工人们在 1820 年“肆意地打破”棺材盖，移开棺材板，寻找埋在死者身边的宝藏。 “1869 年石棺再次打开时所记录的混乱是典型的抢劫行为，但我们永远不会知道是否有任何金属或其他本质上重要的物品存在并被盗，”罗德威尔在论文中解释道。

paras.en: Since the coffin’s rediscovery in the 19th century, it has been moved multiple times, most recently to the Queen’s Diamond Jubilee Galleries, which opened at the abbey in 2018. Although Rodwell writes that its occupant’s identity “cannot be answered with certainty,” he maintains that “the fact that he was honored with a fine sarcophagus, topped with a lid displaying a [5.9-foot-tall] Latin cross, should imply that he was almost certainly an abbot.” As the archaeologist tells the Guardian, “Nobody of lower rank would have been buried in anything like that. The Latin cross again points to a major ecclesiastic.”
paras.zh: 自 19 世纪重新发现棺材以来，它已被多次移动，最近一次被移至 2018 年在修道院开放的女王钻禧画廊。尽管罗德威尔写道，棺材主人的身份“无法确定”，但他坚称“事实上，他获得了一个精致的石棺，顶部的盖子上显示着[5.9英尺高]的雕像”。拉丁十字，应该意味着他几乎肯定是一位修道院院长。”正如考古学家告诉《卫报》的那样，“级别较低的人不会被埋在这样的东西里。拉丁十字再次指向一位主要的教会。”

articles.title: Airbnb Hosts Are Furious They Can No Longer Make Guests Do Their Chores
articles.author: Caroline Haskins

paras.en: Airbnb hosts are melting down over a new policy banning them from making guests complete tasks that “would typically be performed by a cleaner,” like “stripping the bed, taking trash offsite, or washing and putting away dishes.”
paras.zh: Airbnb 的房东对一项新政策感到崩溃，该政策禁止他们让房客完成“通常由清洁工完成的”任务，例如“清理床铺、将垃圾移至异地、清洗和收起餐具”。

paras.en: The change, which applies to all bookings made on or after November 20, quickly sparked outrage after it was announced in an email to Airbnb hosts on Wednesday. Many began fuming online about losing the right to make their guests clean up after themselves.
paras.zh: 这一变化适用于 11 月 20 日或之后进行的所有预订，周三在发给 Airbnb 房东的电子邮件中宣布这一消息后，很快引发了愤怒。许多人开始在网上愤怒地抱怨失去了让客人自己清理干净的权利。

paras.en: “As hosts, we have a responsibility to protect our investments, our homes, and, in many cases, our personal living spaces,” one person wrote in Airbnb’s official forum for hosts. “The problem is that Airbnb increasingly expects hosts to accept the risks while limiting our ability to protect ourselves.”
paras.zh: “作为房东，我们有责任保护我们的投资、我们的房屋，在很多情况下，还有我们的个人生活空间，”一位人士在 Airbnb 的房东官方论坛上写道。 “问题在于，Airbnb 越来越希望房东接受风险，同时限制我们保护自己的能力。”

paras.en: “Airbnb is like an abusive partner,” wrote one user on the Reddit community r/airbnb_hosts. “I'm alive long enough to recognize how truthful those few words are,” another person replied. “Until and unless I see substantive changes, I'm finally out.”
paras.zh: “Airbnb 就像一个施虐的合作伙伴，”Reddit 社区 r/airbnb_hosts 上的一位用户写道。 “我活得够久了，能够认识到这几句话是多么真实，”另一个人回答道。 “除非我看到实质性的变化，否则我最终会退出。”

paras.en: A different self-described host declared that going forward, the kitchens in their rentals will be “stripped down to only bare essentials.”
paras.zh: 另一位自称为房东的人宣称，今后，他们出租的厨房将“精简到只剩下最基本的设施”。

paras.en: Many guests, meanwhile, are celebrating. For years, travelers have complained about having to pay hefty cleaning fees as part of their Airbnb bookings, only to be required to complete a list of chores before checking out.
paras.zh: 与此同时，许多客人正在庆祝。多年来，旅行者一直抱怨在 Airbnb 预订时必须支付高额清洁费，但在退房前却被要求完成一系列家务。

paras.en: “The guest experience has become total ass,” one person said in a subreddit for Airbnb hosts. “Clean dishes and run in the dishwasher. Strip the beds, put all linen in the laundry room. Take out all garbage, put in garbage can, take to the curb. Honestly, knock it off.”
paras.zh: “房客体验已经变得很糟糕，”一位人士在 Airbnb 房东的 Reddit 子版块中说道。 “清洗盘子，然后用洗碗机清洗。把床铺洗干净，把所有床单放在洗衣房里。拿出所有垃圾，放入垃圾桶，带到路边。老实说，把它扔掉。”

paras.en: Airbnb noted in its Wednesday announcement that hosts can’t get around the new policy by putting cleaning tasks in the “Requests” section of their listings instead. Airbnb spokesperson Simon Letouze tells WIRED that hosts can still make “reasonable” requests, such as asking guests to put dirty dishes in the sink. Other examples Airbnb cites include asking guests to take short showers in areas with drought-related water restrictions, or telling them to place trash in bear-proof containers.
paras.zh: Airbnb 在周三的公告中指出，房东无法通过将清洁任务放在房源的“请求”部分来规避新政策。 Airbnb 发言人西蒙·莱图兹 (Simon Letouze) 告诉《连线》杂志，房东仍然可以提出“合理”的要求，例如要求房客将脏盘子放入水槽中。 Airbnb 引用的其他例子包括要求客人在因干旱而限水的地区短暂淋浴，或者告诉他们将垃圾放入防熊容器中。

paras.en: In a Facebook group for Airbnb hosts, one person posted what they claimed was a screenshot of their failed attempt to edit their property’s “Requests” section. They tried to ask guests to wash and air-dry dishes, put dirty towels in the laundry room, and take trash to a dumpster at an RV park they could find using a map on the refrigerator. But they realized they couldn’t hit Save. Airbnb's interface had underlined and highlighted the requests in red and displayed a pop-up that read “Guests shouldn't be asked to do this task.”
paras.zh: 在 Airbnb 房东的 Facebook 群组中，有人发布了一张截图，他们声称这是他们尝试编辑房源“请求”部分失败的截图。他们试图要求客人清洗并风干餐具，将脏毛巾放在洗衣房，并将垃圾扔到他们可以使用冰箱上的地图找到的房车公园的垃圾箱中。但他们意识到他们无法点击“保存”。 Airbnb 的界面用红色下划线突出显示了这些请求，并显示了一个弹出窗口，上面写着“不应要求客人执行此任务”。

paras.en: Hosts also can’t circumvent the new policy by giving guests a printed list of rules and asking them to sign it when they check in. On November 20, Airbnb is also banning hosts from requiring guests to sign separate contracts, with limited exceptions for local legal requirements, longer stays, or accessing “an optional amenity” like a “golf cart rental.”
paras.zh: 房东也不能通过向客人提供打印的规则清单并要求他们在入住时签署来规避新政策。11 月 20 日，Airbnb 还禁止房东要求客人签署单独的合同，但当地法律要求、长期住宿或使用“高尔夫球车租赁”等“可选设施”的情况除外。

paras.en: If one of these situations applies, hosts have to mention it in the dedicated section of their listing. Airbnb adds that it “doesn’t help enforce the terms of these contracts.” Hosts who violate either policy, Airbnb warns, may receive warnings, or in severe situations, have their listings removed or be banned from the platform entirely.
paras.zh: 如果其中一种情况适用，房东必须在房源的专门部分中提及。 Airbnb 补充说，它“无助于执行这些合同的条款。” Airbnb 警告称，违反任何一项政策的房东可能会收到警告，或者在严重的情况下，他们的房源将被删除或完全禁止进入该平台。

paras.en: In a Facebook group for Airbnb hosts, one person posted a letter they claimed to have sent to company executives, demanding the ability to set their own “common-sense expectations” for guests. They encouraged others to send their own versions. Another asked if they should raise their prices, while a third called for hosts to organize a platform-wide strike.
paras.zh: 在 Airbnb 房东的 Facebook 群组中，有人发布了一封自称是发给公司高管的信，要求能够为房客设定自己的“常识性期望”。他们鼓励其他人发送他们自己的版本。另一个人询问他们是否应该提高价格，而第三个人则呼吁房东组织全平台罢工。

paras.en: “Even if we all unlist our properties for just a day or two, we can send a powerful message,” they wrote. “Airbnb built its empire on OUR properties. It’s time we reminded them who actually holds the power.”
paras.zh: 他们写道：“即使我们都将自己的房产取消上市一两天，我们也可以发出强有力的信息。” “Airbnb 在我们的房产上建立了自己的帝国。现在是我们提醒他们谁真正掌握权力的时候了。”

paras.en: Some hosts haven’t given up on finding a way to ignore or get around the changes. On Reddit, one person said they would simply move their rules to other sections of their listing, like “Guest Access.” (Airbnb did not immediately respond to WIRED’s inquiry about whether this would work.) Another person said they would give the guests a “house manual,” require the guest to read it, and provide a “codeword” as proof. (Several pointed out that this is not only unenforceable but against current Airbnb policy.)
paras.zh: 一些主机并没有放弃寻找忽略或绕过这些变化的方法。在 Reddit 上，一位人士表示，他们只需将规则移至列表的其他部分，例如“访客访问”。 （Airbnb 没有立即回应《连线》关于这是否有效的询问。）另一个人表示，他们会给房客一份“房屋手册”，要求房客阅读它，并提供一个“密码”作为证据。 （一些人指出，这不仅无法执行，而且违反了 Airbnb 的现行政策。）

paras.en: “First sentence of my requests section will now state ‘Here are my house rules!’” another person said, though it’s unclear whether Airbnb’s interface will allow this. They named “not smoking” as an example of one of their house rules, but Airbnb has said it enforces host-imposed smoking bans.
paras.zh: “我的请求部分的第一句话现在将注明‘这是我的入住须知！’”另一个人说道，不过目前尚不清楚 Airbnb 的界面是否允许这样做。他们将“禁止吸烟”作为其入住须知之一，但 Airbnb 表示，它会执行房东规定的吸烟禁令。

paras.en: Unwanted smoking and other serious scenarios—like letting dirty dishes become “health hazards,” leaving “permanent stains on sheets,” and creating “mountains of rotting garbage”—were invoked by several hosts. But these policy adjustments, seemingly, will not change how any of these things are treated.
paras.zh: 一些房东提到了不必要的吸烟和其他严重的情况，比如让脏盘子成为“健康隐患”、“床单上留下永久性污渍”以及产生“堆积如山的腐烂垃圾”。但这些政策调整似乎不会改变这些事情的处理方式。

paras.en: Airbnb already has its own ground rules that all guests must agree to. The general credo is to "treat your host’s home like your own," which translates to things like putting trash in the trash can and not leaving moldy dishes.
paras.zh: Airbnb 已经制定了所有房客都必须同意的基本规则。一般的信条是“像对待自己的家一样对待主人的家”，这意味着将垃圾放入垃圾桶，不要留下发霉的盘子。

paras.en: If a host finds that anything was damaged or went missing during a stay, guests are expected to pay a “reasonable” amount to repair or replace it. Hosts are also protected through the platform’s protection program, AirCover, which will reimburse up to $3 million for certain property damage caused by guests, including furniture, cars, and other belongings.
paras.zh: 如果房东发现入住期间有任何物品损坏或丢失，房客需要支付“合理”的费用来修理或更换。房东还可以通过该平台的保护计划 AirCover 获得保护，该计划将为房客造成的某些财产损失提供高达 300 万美元的赔偿，包括家具、汽车和其他物品。

paras.en: Additional cleaning costs, such as performing "smoke odor removal" or handling "pet accidents” are also covered by AirCover. Airbnb notes that the cleaning fees hosts are allowed to set are only meant to cover standard guest turnover tasks like laundry and vacuuming. Hosts can’t “charge guest fees for failing to perform specific cleaning or checkout tasks,” though they can still leave guest reviews “based on cleanliness.”
paras.zh: AirCover 还承担额外的清洁费用，例如执行“烟味去除”或处理“宠物事故”。 Airbnb 指出，房东允许设定的清洁费仅适用于洗衣和吸尘等标准房客周转任务。房东不能“因未能执行特定清洁或结帐任务而向房客收取费用”，但他们仍然可以“根据清洁度”留下房客评价。

paras.en: In the Airbnb Hosts subreddit, a few lurking guests were quick to bring up the cleaning fees, which are famously the subject of their ire. One self-described “mostly guest” said they’re not opposed to running the dishwasher or stripping the bed. “Just don’t charge me a cleaning fee over $100 then,” they said.
paras.zh: 在 Reddit 的 Airbnb Hosts 子版块中，一些潜伏的客人很快就提出了清洁费问题，这是众所周知的他们愤怒的话题。一位自称“主要是客人”的人表示，他们并不反对使用洗碗机或清理床铺。 “那就别向我收取超过 100 美元的清洁费了，”他们说。

paras.en: “Truth nuke,” another person replied. “Why would I have to pre-game the cleaners?”
paras.zh: “真理核武器，”另一个人回答道。 “为什么我必须在比赛前安排清洁工？”

articles.title: Mark Zuckerberg Agrees to Stay in California Despite Billionaires’ Tax Ballot Measure
articles.author: Paresh Dave

paras.en: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg has agreed to keep living in Silicon Valley for eight years, potentially exposing himself to billions of dollars in one-time taxes if California voters approve a contentious ballot measure next month, according to a company regulatory filing released Wednesday.

During a dinner with Meta board members on September 9, Zuckerberg informed them that he was considering leaving California because of the measure, known as Proposition 40, and that he planned to list his Palo Alto, California, home for sale four days later, the 109-page filing stated. The ballot proposal, which could be subject to lawsuits even if voters approve it, calls for a one-time 5 percent tax on stock and other assets held by billionaires in the state as of January 2026.

Many wealthy individuals, including Zuckerberg, currently avoid significant tax payments by borrowing against their shares and taking low salaries—$1 annually in the Meta CEO’s case. Zuckerberg purchased a home in Florida this past February, The Wall Street Journal reported at the time.

His potential cross-country move concerned a special committee of the board, whose members included attorney Robert Kimmitt, venture capitalist Charlie Songhurst, and DoorDash CEO Tony Xu. “The special committee was mindful about the difficulties the company faced during the COVID-19 pandemic when Zuckerberg could not be physically present with the company’s management team and did not want the company to face similar challenges going forward,” according to Wednesday’s filing.
paras.zh: 他潜在的跨国行动涉及董事会的一个特别委员会，该委员会的成员包括律师罗伯特·金米特(Robert Kimmitt)、风险投资家查理·宋赫斯特(Charlie Songhurst)和DoorDash首席执行官托尼·徐(Tony Xu)。根据周三的文件，“特别委员会注意到公司在 COVID-19 大流行期间面临的困难，当时扎克伯格无法亲自与公司管理团队在一起，并且不希望公司今后面临类似的挑战。”

paras.en: Within days of the Meta board dinner, the special committee and Zuckerberg reached an agreement that links his ability to sell special company shares to his continued residence in California. It was finalized a week ago, and on Wednesday, Meta announced the details. It plans to create a new class of shares that hold no voting power. Selling these shares could potentially help raise funds for Meta’s expensive investments in AI data centers, without diluting Zuckerberg’s existing voting control.
paras.zh: 在 Meta 董事会晚宴后的几天内，特别委员会和扎克伯格达成协议，将他出售特殊公司股票的能力与他继续居住在加利福尼亚州联系起来。它在一周前敲定，周三，Meta 宣布了细节。它计划创建一种不具有投票权的新股票类别。出售这些股票可能有助于为 Meta 在人工智能数据中心的昂贵投资筹集资金，而不会削弱扎克伯格现有的投票控制权。

paras.en: All existing shareholders will receive the new nonvoting shares automatically in proportion to their existing holdings. Under what Meta called a “Founder Alignment Agreement” with Zuckerberg, he can sell 20 percent of those new shares to help pay any taxes he may owe. The remaining 80 percent would be available for sale in chunks over the next eight years as long as he remains in California. Any attempt to sell them early would require offloading some of his voting shares “unless there are material unforeseen circumstances that would render it prudent or advisable for Zuckerberg to reside elsewhere.”
paras.zh: 所有现有股东将按照其现有持股比例自动获得新的无投票权股份。根据 Meta 所说的与扎克伯格达成的“创始人联盟协议”，他可以出售 20% 的新股，以帮助支付他可能欠下的任何税款。只要他留在加州，剩下的 80% 的土地就可以在未来八年内分批出售。任何提前出售这些股份的尝试都需要出售他的部分投票权股份，“除非出现重大的不可预见的情况，使扎克伯格居住在其他地方变得谨慎或明智”。

paras.en: Notably, the agreement specifies that Zuckerberg merely has to remain wherever Meta maintains its headquarters, so it’s possible that both he and the company could move together to another state. A number of California companies have left for Texas, Nevada, and other states in recent years. Google cofounders Sergey Brin and Larry Page are among the handful of billionaires widely believed to have exited California over the potential tax.
paras.zh: 值得注意的是，该协议规定扎克伯格只需留在 Meta 总部所在的地方，因此他和公司有可能一起搬到另一个州。近年来，许多加州公司已迁往德克萨斯州、内华达州和其他州。谷歌联合创始人谢尔盖·布林（Sergey Brin）和拉里·佩奇（Larry Page）是被广泛认为因潜在税收而离开加州的少数亿万富翁之一。

paras.en: But with much of the most pioneering AI development happening in Silicon Valley, leaving the city of Menlo Park could be a difficult proposition for the Meta board to stomach. “The goal is to keep Zuckerberg continuing to lead the company from California and in close proximity to Meta Superintelligence Labs,” the filing stated, referring to the company unit behind its recent Muse AI models.
In the end, the exercise may have been for naught. Recent polling in California suggests that with about $129 million spent campaigning against Prop 40, it will fail to muster enough votes.
paras.zh: 最终，这次演习可能毫无意义。加州最近的民意调查显示，反对 40 号提案的竞选花费了约 1.29 亿美元，但该提案将无法获得足够的选票。

articles.title: Hackers Exploited the PHP Vulnerabilities Days Before They Were Patched
articles.author: Lily Hay Newman

paras.en: The internet’s mad scramble on Wednesday to patch a pair of critical vulnerabilities in PHP, a widely used web scripting language, was already too late to stop every attack, newly released details reveal.

Wednesday’s release of fixes for two critical vulnerabilities in PHP caused administrators and security staff to race to identify and patch vulnerable websites and apps, while attackers inevitably reverse engineered the fixes to learn how to exploit the flaws. Some governments and other groups even proactively took key websites down in anticipation of the release, so they wouldn't be targeted before they could apply the patches.

But in addition to detecting such active exploitation on Wednesday, research published Wednesday evening by Amazon Web Services indicates that at least one actor had started attempting to exploit the bugs—known collectively as PHP2Shell—on October 17, four days before Wednesday's public revelations.

AWS analysts spotted the October 17 exploitation on Wednesday while looking back at activity on one of their so-called honeypots, or intentionally vulnerable web servers or other digital lures that help researchers study attack methods and trends. The attempt came from an IP address that AWS says is linked to a “commercial anonymization network,” in other words a proxy network or VPN.

“While the vulnerability was under embargo, the targeting of a honeypot from an anonymized IP address suggests the activity was conducted by a threat actor, though it remains unclear how the actor acquired exploit information prior to disclosure,” CJ Moses, AWS's chief information security officer, wrote in the research post.

Proof-of-concept exploits for PHP2Shell began emerging publicly on Wednesday, with some seeming to appear hours before the public disclosure at 10 am ET. In the hours leading up to the disclosure, AWS researchers say their honeypots were hit with multiple exploitation attempts anonymized using various providers and seemingly with various attack goals, likely indicating multiple different actors. “Technical analysis is ongoing, and it’s unclear if any of these attempts would have succeeded in real-world systems,” Moses wrote. He added that “PHP2Shell is now being broadly exploited in the wild.”

paras.en: The PHP Foundation did not immediately respond to WIRED's request for comment.

Though it is unclear how the exploitation on October 17 happened or where it came from, AWS emphasizes that the findings underscore how coordinated vulnerability disclosure must evolve and speed up given global access to AI tools that can accelerate vulnerability analysis and allow less technically proficient actors to quickly develop new exploits.

“The time from patch to working exploit is shrinking for structural reasons,” Moses wrote. “In the past, most exploitation we observed came after a public proof of concept was released. A small number of capable actors built exploits, and everyone else waited for them. That dependency is weakening. AI-assisted analysis makes it cheaper to turn a patch diff or advisory into a working exploit. As a result, more actors can act within hours or even minutes once technical details of a vulnerability are disclosed.”

articles.title: DOJ accuses OSU Med of discriminating against White, Asian applicants

paras.en: Oct. 21 (UPI) -- Federal lawyers on Wednesday accused Ohio State University College of Medicine of operating an admissions program that discriminates against White and Asian applicants, the latest investigative finding in the Trump administration's campaign to eliminate diversity, equity and inclusion policies at institutions of higher learning.

The Justice Department's Civil Rights Division has opened dozens of investigations into federally funded universities concerning compliance with a 2023 Supreme Court ruling that restricted race-conscious admissions practices.

In announcing the findings of its investigation into OSU Med, the Justice Department said it discriminated against White and Asian students in granting admission to its 2023, 2024 and 2025 incoming classes, in violation of Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, as interpreted by a Supreme Court's 2023 ruling, which prohibits discrimination based on race or national origin in federally funded programs.
Ohio State told UPI in an emailed statement that it "strongly disagrees with the findings."

In a letter to the university, the Justice Department said Ohio State's medical school intentionally discriminated in its admissions process while pursuing its stated goal of including students from "historically excluded and underserved groups," resulting in discrimination "against certain applicants, particularly Asians, to benefit preferred race classes of Black and Hispanic."

According to its findings, the Justice Department said OSU Med has practiced a "holistic approach" to admissions since 2011 to increase admissions of underrepresented minorities. While the school says it considers an applicant's attributes, experiences and metrics, including GPA and MCAT scores, equally, federal lawyers allege it gives greater weight to attributes and experiences to favor Black and Hispanic applicants.

The Justice Department alleges that OSU Med also uses so-called Super Screeners, admissions reviewers who can see applicants' race and ethnicity, to favor those groups. It said Black applicants with similar academic credentials had 7.7 times the odds of advancing to the interview stage as Asian applicants and 4.6 times the odds as White applicants in the 2025 admissions cycle. Hispanic applicants had 2.3 times the odds of being interviewed as White or Asian applicants with similar academic credentials, it said.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: The department also alleges that OSU Med operates a so-called side door admissions process, allowing some applicants to bypass the initial screening and the standard admissions committee review. According to the findings, Black applicants who used this pathway were four times as likely to be admitted as White applicants with comparable academic credentials during the 2024 and 2025 admissions cycles, while no Asian applicants were admitted through it.
It also accused the school of using socioeconomic disadvantage scores as a substitute for race to favor underrepresented minority applicants.

"A university's admissions process, and all its stages, should apply equally to all applicants regardless of race," Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon of the Justice Department's Civil Rights Division said in a statement.

"The use of a separate admissions process based on race is plainly illegal under federal law, and this department will not allow these appalling practices to continue at OSU Med or any other federally funded higher ed institution."
The Justice Department is seeking to enter a voluntary resolution agreement with the university to ensure that its admissions practices are brought into legal compliance.

In disagreeing with the Justice Department's assessment, Ohio State told UPI that it was in full compliance with the Supreme Court's 2023 ruling and all federal and state laws and regulations regarding admissions.
"The College of Medicine does not consider race, ethnicity or any other protected class during the admissions process," it said. "Ohio State follows the law and will contest these findings."

The Justice Department's Civil Rights Division has launched more than 100 investigations into the admissions processes of federally funded universities in line with executive orders signed by President Donald Trump seeking to eliminate DEI policies, arguing that it seeks to reestablish merit-based practices in these institutions.
The Trump administration has announced similar findings involving at least seven other medical schools and at least three law schools.

articles.title: Edwards, Timberwolves spoil Antetokounmpo's Heat debut

paras.en: MIAMI, Oct. 21 (UPI) -- Anthony Edwards' orchestral rhythm vanquished defenders and hushed hype of Giannis Antetokounmpo's Miami Heat debut in a lopsided Minnesota Timberwolves triumph Wednesday in Miami.

The Timberwolves star poured in 45 points in the 131-106 victory at Kaseya Center. Antetokounmpo supplied 35, setting a record for the most points scored by a player in his Heat debut. But his Eurostep steps and sky-scraping slams weren't enough to help the Heat keep pace with the vicious visitors.
Edwards made 16 of 29 shots. He sank more 3-pointers (9 of 17) than the entire Heat roster (8 of 33). Meanwhile, Antetokounmpo made 13 of 19 attempts. He scored 21 points in the first half.

"It became Edwards dribble-dance and trying to get to his air space," Heat coach Erik Spoelstra said. "He felt comfortable all night long. We never got him thinking about anything else other than the rim.
"We are going to have to step up our defense. We know that."

The Heat outshot the Timberwolves 48.1% to 46.9%, but their poor 3-point clip (24.2%) and inability to slow Edwards stoked their demise. They also trailed 52-34 in rebounding and 20 to 6 in second-chance points.
All seven of the game's lead changes occurred in the first half. The Timberwolves, who led by as many as 30 points, outscored the Heat 62-47 in the second.

Antetokounmpo steamed from tip off, scoring the Heat's first eight points. He went on to total 14 over the first 12 minutes. But the Timberwolves carried a 34-32 lead into the second quarter. They outscored the Heat 35-27 over the next dozen minutes, including a 14-5 run to end the half.

Edwards splashed in another 15 points in the third quarter, when the Timberwolves outscored the Heat 30-22. He added nine in the final frame to help seal the Timberwolves' first win of the season. He chipped in 10 rebounds, in addition to his 45 points.

Timberwolves guard LaMelo Ball scored 21 points. Forward Jaden McDaniels supplied 17. Heat center Bam Adebayo scored 15 points in the loss. Point guard Davion Mitchell contributed 11 points and 11 assists.
Antetokounmpo and the Heat (0-1) will host the Detroit Pistons (1-0) at 7 p.m. EDT Friday in Miami. The Timberwolves (1-0) will take on the Orlando Magic (0-1) at 7 p.m. Friday in Orlando, Fla.

articles.title: Israeli forces detain New York congressional candidate in West Bank

paras.en: Oct. 21 (UPI) -- New York City congressional candidate Brad Lander said Wednesday that he was detained in the occupied West Bank by the Israeli military as he volunteered to help with the olive harvest in the Palestinian territory.
In a post on X, Lander said: "I've been detained by the IDF, along with a group of rabbis & volunteers."
He said they were "simply harvesting olives in a grove" in the West Bank.
The Democrat shared a photo of himself on a bus with the other detainees.
"The occupation is a crime under international law. Harvesting olives isn't a crime under any law I know," he added.
He later posted that he had been released because he is a congressional candidate, but that others were still detained.
Lander, who is Jewish, is a former New York City comptroller running for Congress in New York's 10th Congressional District. He was in Israel with the Protect the Harvest organization.
In a phone interview, Lander told The New York Times that he had been detained for about three hours and then released.

"I was eventually released and I was told I was being given a warning, that my actions were illegal and wrong, and that we had created a public disturbance and gone where we weren't supposed to go," Lander said in an interview from Beit Jala in the West Bank.
Lander told The Times that he protested his release.
"I hadn't done anything different from anyone else, and I certainly didn't deserve any special treatment," he said.
"The rabbis and others are still there in detention, and we don't know -- obviously they're under threat of deportation, and all we were doing was harvesting olives," he said.

The steering committee for Protect the Harvest said the international volunteers were being held at the Etzion military base and the Israeli detainees were held at the Beitar Illit police station, both in the occupied West Bank.
Lander said that on Monday and Tuesday, the group had harvested olives in another area of the West Bank without incident.
The trip was organized in part by Israelis for Peace and Rabbis for Human Rights. Lander said there were about 60 volunteers in the group, including 40 foreign nationals, who were mostly Americans.

Violence against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank has surged recently, with attacks on international diplomats and journalists. On Monday, Israeli police arrested 10 people accused of attacking two groups of people in the olive harvest.

Israel's occupation of the West Bank is widely seen as illegal under international law, and Lander's detention comes amid increasing Israeli settlement activity in the occupied West Bank, including the E1 development project, which critics warn would further divide Palestinian communities and undermine prospects for a future Palestinian state.

Israel's Foreign Ministry on Wednesday criticized Lander's volunteer work as being more about creating headlines than harvesting olives, calling it a "stunt" that was "nothing more than a calculated political provocation."

"Lander traveled to a foreign country, deliberately entered a restricted security area and participated in an unauthorized activity without the required coordination," the ministry said in a statement.
"Had anyone been injured as a result of his reckless political theater, Lander would undoubtedly have been among the first to demand that Israeli authorities intervene and provide protection."
Lander responded to the ministry, saying he and the other volunteers were not in a restricted area, did not pass any checkpoints and were not told coordination was necessary to harvest olives.
"We're trying to model solidarity & co-existence between Jews and Palestinians, and to call attention to the horrors of the occupation," Lander said in a statement.

"The Israeli government is trying to foment violence between Jews and Palestinians, and to make it impossible for Palestinians to harvest their olive groves, drive on their roads or live in their homes."

Meanwhile, fellow Democrats came to Lander's defense, with New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani stating "Harvesting olives is not illegal. The occupation is," and Rep. Pramila Jayapal of Washington saying his arrest "is a stark reminder of the abuses Palestinians face on a near daily basis."

articles.title: Rubén Blades Reflects on His Legacy at Latin Music Week: ‘What I Wrote Was Honest & I Still Feel That Way’
articles.author: Sigal Ratner-Arias

paras.en: Colombian Nobel Prize in Literature winner Gabriel García Márquez considered himself more of a writer than a singer, says Rubén Blades. But the legendary Panamanian singer/songwriter sees himself more as a “journalist” who “tries to be as objective as possible within the subjectivity of creating a song.”

“What I wrote was honest and I still feel that way,” Blades said on Wednesday (Oct. 21) during the Icon Q&A With Rubén Blades panel, moderated by Billboard‘s co-chief content officer Leila Cobo at Billboard Latin Music Week.

Entire generations across Latin America and the U.S. have grown up listening to Blades, one of salsa’s most influential voices, who helped redefine the genre with a unique combination of musical innovation and powerful storytelling. A central figure in New York City’s salsa revolution of the 70s, Blades expanded the horizons of classic Afro-Cuban salsa by incorporating influences from rock, jazz, Pan-Latin music and sounds from various parts of the world.

“Music offers many varieties; not everything has to be political or critical — it’s also for having fun and dancing,” he noted. “My contribution was believing that music didn’t necessarily have to talk about the same themes — betrayal by a woman or a friend — but could go beyond that.”

This is how his songs have stood out, not only for their unforgettable melodies but also for their socially conscious lyrics and memorable characters. He turned stories of everyday life into timeless music, with classics such as “Pedro Navaja,” “Decisiones” and “El Padre Antonio y Su Monaguillo Andrés.”

At 78, Blades remains very active in music, touring across the region and working on various acting projects. These include his recent appearance in the movie Campeón Gabacho by Mexican filmmaker Jonás Cuarón and his upcoming role in Porto Rico, the first fiction feature film directed by René Pérez (Residente), which also marks Latin music superstar Bad Bunny’s debut as a lead actor.

“What [Residente] is doing is extremely interesting,” Blades said without revealing details about his role in the film. “We both share the same curiosity — I learn from him, he learns from Bad Bunny, and from Viggo Mortensen too. We’re learning from everyone, and René is learning from them now.”

During the talk, Blades also reminisced about the last time he spoke with his former collaborator Willie Colón, who passed away on February 21, 2023. The two had a long-standing dispute over the Siembra 25 Años concert (2003) and the master rights related to it. Blades shared that the last time they met was in 2023 at the wake of musician Jorge “Georgie” González.

“It was a cordial meeting,” recalled Blades, who is also a lawyer and Panama’s former Minister of Tourism. “The last photos we took together were that afternoon. My respect and recognition for him will never disappear.”

This Thursday (Oct. 22), Blades will be honored with the Billboard Icon Award at the 2026 Billboard Latin Music Awards, which will be broadcast live on Telemundo from Miami. The award recognizes an artist whose career has not only remained relevant over time but has also established them as one of the most distinguished artists in their genre, celebrated worldwide for achieving both musical and commercial success.

Blades, whose career spans more than five decades, said he still feels energized to continue touring — even performing five-and-a-half-hour shows, as he did during a concert in Puerto Rico. “I think the only surprise is that I don’t know how to drive,” he confessed, adding that it’s not something he plans to learn at this stage of his life.

articles.title: John Anderson, Country Music Hall of Fame Inductee, Dies at 71
articles.author: Lars Brandle

paras.en: John Anderson, the Country Music Hall of Fame inductee with a distinctive voice and a weighty songbook that included “Swingin’,” “Straight Tequila Night,” and “Seminole Wind,” died today (Oct. 21) at the age of 71.
“It is with the heaviest of hearts that we share the passing of our beloved husband, father, grandfather, and best friend,” reads a statement from his family.

Anderson, who attended the Country Music Hall of Fame induction ceremony to herald this year’s honorees on Sunday (Oct. 18), died peacefully in his sleep, reads the statement from his family, roughly seven weeks before his 72nd birthday. “His music will live on, but for us, his greatest legacy will always be the love he gave his family and the memories we will carry with us forever. Please keep our family in your thoughts and prayers as we grieve this unimaginable loss.”

“To the world, he was a gifted country music singer whose voice and songs touched countless lives. To us, he was so much more. He was the heart of our family, the one who made us laugh, loved us fiercely, and made every ordinary moment feel special. We are completely heartbroken.”

His fellow country artists were remembering him as a singular talent. “There is too much for me to say about John Anderson in just a statement,” posted Blake Shelton on X. “I am sick and I am stunned. But I am a very lucky man. I got the opportunity to find out that my hero wasn’t just the guy I hoped he’d be. He was so much more than that. John was my friend.”
John Rich called Anderson “my favorite country artist of all time…He was a massive influence on me in more ways that I can count. I love you, Uncle John.”
A native of Apopka, Fla., Anderson relocated to Nashville in 1971. An early job saw him nailing shingles onto the roof of the Grand Ole Opry House ahead of that iconic building’s 1974 opening.

“I was just wanting to play and sing pretty much at any level that I could,” he told Billboard in 2024. “Thankfully, I was blessed that one little job led to another one, and most of the time it was kind of a little upgrade.”

That upgrade came when he signed with Warner Bros. Records and went about constructing a lofty career in music with such works as “I’m Just an Old Chunk of Coal (But I’m Gonna Be a Diamond Someday),” “Wild and Blue,” “I Just Came Home to Count the Memories,” “1959,” “Black Sheep,” and his signature song “Swingin’, which would scoop both the CMA Horizon Award and single of the year in 1983.

Anderson’s hot start cooled for a time, but his career took off once again when he signed with BNA in 1991 and landed a comeback hit with the Country Airplay chart-topping “Straight Tequila Night,” housed on his album Seminole Wind.

A neo-traditional pioneer, Anderson was both a critical and commercial success. He landed five No. 1s, among 20 top 10s, on Billboard‘s Hot Country Songs chart, with those top 10s spanning 1981-95. On Top Country Albums, he notched five top 10s, from the years 1982-92. Respect came from his peers, too, with Academy of Country Music’s career achievement award in 1993, induction into the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame in 2014, and entry into the Country Music Hall of Fame a decade later, in 2024.

paras.en: Anderson battled health issues in recent years, but pushed through the pain. “Through all of 2017 and all the way up until May of 2018, I had spent most of my time in the hospital and had been very, very ill,” he told Billboard in 2020. “I had almost 100% hearing loss. I did OK being sick, but when I lost my hearing and couldn’t play and sing, that really almost put an end to me. I just started praying and praying harder than I’ve ever prayed in my life and you know what? My hearing started coming back.”

paras.en: During one procedure, he says he almost died on the operating room table. Anderson, however, was a hard man to stop. During the peak of the pandemic, he released an album of new material, Years, produced by The Black Keys’ Dan Auerbach and David “Fergie” Ferguson.

“John Anderson was a one-of-a-kind song stylist who proved that fresh innovations were best born from time-honored traditions,” recounts Kyle Young, CEO of the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum. “Whether he borrowed inspiration from Lefty Frizzell’s vocal bends or the Florida swamp land, he brought dynamic distinction and creative soul to a world that needed to hear his voice. In 1981, John famously gave life to Billy Joe Shaver’s lyric, ‘I’m just an old chunk of coal, but I’ll be a diamond someday.’ He was already a diamond then, and a diamond he always will be.”
