articles.title: U.S. Light-Vehicle Sales Expected to Remain Low
articles.author: Christian Hinton

paras.en: U.S. light-vehicle sales are projected to reach 16.1 million units in 2026 and 16.4 million by 2030, according to Mobility Global’s latest forecast. That remains below the roughly 17 million annual sales that characterized the pre-pandemic market. Analysts at a recent Mobility Global media briefing cited affordability as the key constraint shaping buyer demand and automaker strategy.
U.S. Light-Vehicle Sales Remain Below Potential
The market has struggled to return to pre-pandemic volume despite improved supply conditions. Analysts said affordability is now the primary factor limiting recovery.

“We don’t see the U.S. returning to pre-pandemic levels of volumes,” said Peter Nagle, associate director for Americas demand forecasting. “Obviously, there is something constraining the market from those 17-million-unit thresholds that we routinely hit back in, say, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019.”
BEV Programs Shift as Hybrids Gain Share
Analysts noted that recent changes to emissions and fuel economy rules have prompted automakers to adjust product plans.

“The resulting wave of battery-electric vehicle (BEV) cancellations may leave some suppliers wary of chasing future BEV programs,” said Eric Anderson, associate director for light vehicle powertrain forecasting.

Even so, Mobility Global said it expects North American BEV assembly to surpass 1 million units in 2027. Internal combustion engine vehicles and hybrids are expected to remain central to the market as buyers weigh cost and convenience.

The firm forecasts North American full hybrid electric vehicle (FHEV) assembly to exceed 3 million units in 2027. That would represent a 25% annual increase. Forecasts project FHEVs will account for nearly one-third of North American light-vehicle assembly by 2030.

Shifts in the powertrain mix can affect service bay needs. These include tire selection and load ratings for electrified vehicles, along with alignment and brake service intervals linked to regenerative braking and vehicle mass.
Regionalization Shapes Global Strategies
Analysts discussed China’s influence on global strategies and a broader trend toward regionalization and de-globalization.

“The auto industry is moving toward three major regional islands,” said Joe Langley, director of research and analysis. “North America, Europe and Asia, and automakers will increasingly have to build where they sell and design for the regions they serve. The difficult part is doing that while costs continue to rise.”

Mobility Global launched FAST (Forecasting and Simulation Tool) to help organizations evaluate market shifts. Mobility Global, a provider of automotive data, intelligence and forecasting, separated from S&P Global on July 1. It now operates as an independent company focused on the mobility sector.

“We are seeing firsthand that certainty is becoming increasingly rare, and the ability to navigate uncertainty with speed is becoming the most valuable competitive advantage in this market,” said Kristen Balasia, senior vice president of Mobility Global Planning Solutions.

articles.title: Mini Cooper Clutch Replacement
articles.author: ImportCar Staff Writers

paras.en: The subject vehicle today is a 2014 Mini Cooper Countryman AWD, with a six-speed manual transmission. Mini is one of the only makes that the large local dealership it originally came to does not sell; being in good standing with this dealership, they brought it to us to perform the repairs needed and get their customer back on the road. With very little information available on the internet for removal and installation, we did think about purchasing a short-term subscription to BMW/Mini service information, but hey, it’s a clutch job so how hard could it be?
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: The vehicle needed a clutch replacement, which seemed fairly straight forward, so we jumped right in to get this back to the customer as quickly as we possibly could. We ended up needing to call the local Mini dealer and order OE parts since there was limited availability of aftermarket clutch parts. This vehicle was equipped with a Dual Mass Flywheel set up, so with this knowledge we started the removal process. Remove the air box, get the battery out of the way, removed the bell housing bolts, etc., all from the engine compartment, then raise the vehicle up to start taking off the front two wheels. Also, a good trick we found was taking the driver’s side head light out, and removing the front bumper cover as this gave us better access to the transmission and it was removed fairly easily and quickly, we felt that this added step saved us a lot of time not trying to fight getting access in such a tight area. After this, things started to get interesting.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Figure 1 shows the rear driveshaft where it attaches to the Power Transfer Unit. We discovered a TSB that referred to this attachment. It told us we needed a special tool to get it apart and it is a large wrench end that attaches to a long half-inch extension to get it apart (Figure 2). We obviously did not have anything even remotely close to this tool, nor did any of our other shops in the area. Calling the local dealer, we could buy the special tool, but it was a little over a week out to get one. Upon further investigation we decided the PTU possibly could come out with the driveshaft still attached.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: After unbolting the PTU and separating it from the transmission we found the next road block: the intermediate shaft in the PTU is too long to get the PTU removed without it hitting the back of the engine. We started looking over how everything is put together, to see if we could still make this work. While looking, we found a snap ring around the passenger side axle (Figure 3). With that snap ring removed (and with the help of a sharp, new pry bar, and hammer) the axle popped out of the PTU, allowing us to remove that PTU with the driveshafts still attached. This might not be the easiest method, but it worked, and we transmission technicians always seem to find a way to get ’er done!
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Figure 4 shows the PTU on the floor with the attached pieces mentioned. After getting these parts out of the way, we could then remove the transmission. As a side note, if you do need to service the driveshaft for any reason, you will need that special tool I mentioned previously to get the driveshaft separated from the PTU. Back on track, everything else went very smoothly and we finished replacing the clutch, flywheel and all associated parts. We put the vehicle back together, and then went for that final test drive.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Some additional notes: Make sure the correct parts are ordered for these vehicles and the labor charge is sufficient. This was a very big clutch job, and very expensive as the total bill came out to be around $2,700 retail. Make sure if it is supposed to have a Dual Mass Flywheel (DMF) it gets replaced, trying to cut corners on a job like this does not do you or your customer any good. Not pricing this job out correctly up front can mean one of those phone calls that you do not want to make after the vehicle is disassembled. It can mean a very large pricing difference, as well as correct fitments.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: This is where the LUK clutch catalog or online catalog can come in handy with this catalog you can check to see if they offer the DMF set up for your application. LUK offers a much more affordable option for your customers versus the OE parts (for many applications, LUK or Valeo are the OE supplier), so you will save your customer quite a bit of money if your application is available from them. In their catalog, you can also find the “flywheel options” if you are sending out the flywheel to be surfaced, as the information in the catalog will tell you if it is a flat, step, DMF (cannot be turned), or cupped style. It will give you dimensions and measurements so you can make sure the flywheel will still be in spec after having it surfaced.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: In closing, I just want to say if you get one of these all-wheel drive Mini Coopers in your shop, do not turn it away for fear of being too complicated. The job ended up being fairly easy, the shop made good money, and the R&R technician made good time on it. Next time he will be able to do it even faster, and have an even better turnaround time.

articles.title: Turning ADAS Calibration into a Competitive Advantage
articles.author: ImportCar Staff Writers

paras.en: See how Zimbrick of Madison transformed its approach to ADAS calibration by bringing more of the process in-house. With three body shops, 16 automotive brands and a centralized glass and calibration center, Zimbrick partnered with National Calibration and Diagnostic Solutions (NCDS) and Autel to build a more controlled and scalable calibration workflow. The video explores how the right equipment, training and support can help collision repair facilities improve efficiency, documentation, repair quality and customer communication while keeping up with increasingly complex vehicle technology.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: - Bringing ADAS calibration in-house: Zimbrick reduced its reliance on outside vendors to gain greater control over scanning, calibration and the overall repair process.
- Centralizing calibration services: A hub-and-spoke model allows three body shops to work with a centralized calibration center while maintaining consistent processes.
- Improving repair quality and accountability: In-house capabilities give Zimbrick greater visibility into technician training, OEM procedures, documentation and how calibrations are completed.
- Combining glass and calibration: Locating glass replacement and ADAS calibration together allows Zimbrick to complete more windshield installations and calibrations on the same day.
- Training the entire team: Education extends beyond technicians to estimators, helping staff better understand ADAS requirements and explain necessary procedures to customers.

- Building customer confidence: Employees can explain why a calibration is required, what equipment is being used and how the procedure fits into a complete repair rather than simply presenting an additional charge.

- Getting more from ADAS technology: Autel equipment provides diagnostic, calibration and documentation capabilities, while NCDS provides tooling recommendations, training, workflow guidance and ongoing technical support.

- Creating a scalable operation: With approximately 400 repair orders moving through the operation each month, bringing scans and calibrations under Zimbrick’s control helps turn a necessary repair procedure into an opportunity for greater efficiency and additional in-house service.

articles.title: How the Alignment Process is Changing
articles.author: Andrew Markel

paras.en: If you were working in an alignment pit before the 1980s, obtaining the initial angles was a relatively easy process because most vehicles had steel wheels. Mounting the alignment “sensor” with rim clamps provided a very accurate representation of the front wheels’ planes of rotation for measuring camber, caster and toe. However, because the tools used to measure these angles were contained inside the sensor head, they were very fragile and frequently fell out of calibration.

By the 1980s, more vehicles were being equipped with cast-alloy wheels that did not have a suitable lip for mounting the sensor head. Getting a secure grip on the rim became more difficult. It was not uncommon for a rim clamp to come off during an alignment and damage the expensive head.

In the 1990s, alignment technology began to change with improvements in digital cameras. Engineers started mounting cameras to fixtures positioned in front of the vehicle. The expensive sensors at the wheels were replaced with simple targets that the cameras could scan to determine the alignment angles.
However, cameras added a new wrinkle to the alignment process: the rolling-compensation procedure. This procedure also helped resolve problems caused by attaching alignment targets to alloy wheels.

Nearly every modern chassis alignment system uses this step to obtain accurate alignment measurements. First, the vehicle is positioned 12 to 20 inches behind the front turntables. Most systems require the targets to be attached so that a specified part of each target is level with the center of the wheel. The vehicle is then rolled forward onto the turntables. This process is called rolling compensation.
Modern camera-based aligners attach a target to each wheel, and the vehicle is rolled backward or forward a short distance while the cameras track each target through part of a wheel revolution.

As the wheel rotates, the aligner observes the path traveled by the target. The system detects changes in the target’s orientation or the center of the wheel’s rotation caused by clamp runout, wheel damage or an off-center target. From these observations, the software calculates the relationship between the target and the wheel’s actual plane of rotation. This prevents a slightly crooked clamp or target from being interpreted as camber or toe.

The primary purpose of rolling compensation is to establish the true rotational plane and centerline of each wheel while compensating for target or clamp mounting errors. Camber and toe can then be calculated directly. Caster and steering-axis inclination require a separate steering sweep.

Some systems do not require rolling compensation. These systems typically use lasers, mirrors or other devices mounted near the center of the lift to calculate the alignment angles. On some heavy-duty alignment systems, the target or sensor is mounted directly to the spindle.
With today’s electronic parking brakes and advanced driver-assistance systems, including collision-mitigation systems, the alignment process is becoming more challenging.

Even pulling a vehicle onto an alignment rack can be a struggle. We recently had a 2024 Audi Q4 come into our training center. As the technician began driving the vehicle onto the ramps of the drive-on lift, the car applied the brakes, stopped and displayed a collision warning on the instrument panel. The technician applied the accelerator, and the vehicle eventually began moving again.

Even after reviewing the service information, it was unclear what caused this behavior. Was the alignment equipment interfering with the vehicle’s sensors, or was the system reacting to the proximity of the wall and toolbox in front of the vehicle? Were the lasers on the cameras causing the issue?

We had a similar incident with a 2023 Ford F-150 that bucked like a bronco (not a Ford Bronco) while we were positioning it on a drive-on lift. Once again, neither the service information nor the owner’s manual clearly explained the behavior.

Most other late-model vehicles with collision-mitigation systems that we have driven onto the same lift issue audible and visual warnings when they detect what they interpret as a possible threat in the bay. However, they rarely intervene and stop the vehicle.

Even more challenging are the procedures for preparing a vehicle for an alignment when it must be moved during rolling compensation. The primary difficulties involve keeping the parking brake released and the transmission in neutral.

Many modern vehicles use electronic parking brakes that engage automatically when the vehicle is parked. Some systems do this for safety, while others use the parking brake to prevent slight vehicle movement before the transmission’s parking pawl fully engages.
Even if the transmission is placed in neutral and the ignition is switched off using a push button or physical key, the parking brake may engage automatically without any action from the driver.

On many vehicles, the driver’s gear selection does not have final authority. Even after neutral is selected, a control module may shift the transmission into park when it detects certain conditions, such as an open driver’s door or an unbuckled seat belt.

Modern transmissions use electronic driver interfaces and communicate with numerous other vehicle systems. This integration has made selecting neutral—and keeping the transmission in neutral—more challenging.

Working around systems designed to protect the driver requires awareness, accurate information and, in some cases, a scan tool. Many vehicles have built-in procedures or operating modes that allow them to remain in neutral and roll freely. The challenge is finding the correct procedure.

Many late-model Ford vehicles have a Stay in Neutral or Temporary Neutral mode that remains active for a limited period. Depending on the vehicle, the mode may be engaged by holding the brake pedal, selecting neutral and pressing the manual-mode or low-range button when prompted.

Some Tesla alignment procedures require the technician to buckle the front seat belts and manually close the front door latches before placing the vehicle in neutral. This prevents the vehicle from determining that the occupants have exited and automatically applying park or the electronic parking brake.

Other vehicles allow technicians to activate these modes through the infotainment system. Some require a particular sequence of button presses to keep the transmission in neutral and the electronic parking brake released. Instructions for these procedures may be found in the service information or owner’s manual.

In other cases, a scan tool with bidirectional controls or dedicated service functions may be needed to select neutral, place the braking system in a service mode or release the electronic parking brake. Regardless of the method, technicians must follow the manufacturer’s instructions and use wheel chocks whenever the vehicle is not being moved for the rolling-compensation procedure.

It is easy to see that alignment and ADAS calibration are beginning to merge into a single service as chassis alignment and ADAS sensor positioning become increasingly dependent on each other. One area that is currently growing is the integration of vehicle communication capabilities into the alignment and calibration bay. As more late-model vehicles come out of warranty, alignment service will require an even more increased use of scan tools to initiate adjustments and calibrations.

articles.title: Recalling The Brake Rotor Wars of the Early 2000s
articles.author: Andrew Markel

paras.en: Last year, Chinese and Turkish brake drum manufacturers were hit with antidumping duties for selling some trailer brake drums in the United States at less than fair market value. The news gave me flashbacks to the light-vehicle rotor market 25 years ago, when I first started working on Brake & Front End magazine.
paras.zh: 去年，中国和土耳其的制动鼓制造商因在美国以低于公平市场价值的价格销售一些拖车制动鼓而受到反倾销税的打击。这个消息让我回想起25年前的轻型汽车转子市场，当时我刚开始从事《制动与前端》杂志的工作。

paras.en: In the early 2000s, shops faced brake pedal pulsation comebacks for several reasons. Some people might call it a perfect storm.
paras.zh: 在21世纪初，由于几个原因，商店面临着刹车踏板脉动的卷土重来。有些人可能会称之为完美风暴。

paras.en: Facing new fuel-efficiency standards, OEMs began removing mass from brake rotors. Vehicles such as the Jeep Cherokee and Chevrolet Malibu used “composite” rotor designs with stamped-steel hats cast into iron friction rings. These rotors would develop lateral runout if the lug nuts were tightened even slightly unevenly.
paras.zh: 面对新的燃油效率标准，原始设备制造商开始从制动转子中去除质量。吉普切诺基(Jeep Cherokee)和雪佛兰马里布(Chevrolet Malibu)等车辆采用“复合”转子设计，将冲压钢帽铸成铁摩擦环。如果凸耳螺母稍微不均匀地拧紧，这些转子会产生横向跳动。

paras.en: Some rotor manufacturers introduced one-piece replacements for these composite applications, but wheel-stud length was always a concern. Because the cast hats were thicker, the studs sometimes did not extend far enough beyond the rotor flange to properly secure the wheel. Some aftermarket brake companies even offered longer wheel-stud kits.
paras.zh: 一些转子制造商为这些复合材料应用引入了单件更换，但轮毂螺栓长度一直是一个问题。由于铸造帽较厚，螺栓有时延伸到转子法兰之外不足以正确固定车轮。一些售后市场的制动器公司甚至提供了更长的车轮螺栓套件。

paras.en: This period also marked the infancy of ceramic brake pad formulations. Most OE friction materials at the start of the transition process were semi-metallic or aggressive non-asbestos organic (NAO) compounds that could contribute to disc thickness variation when even a small amounts of runout were present. Ceramic formulations were being rolled out that on new OE platforms and as aftermarket alternatives. They can be credited, at least in part, with extending rotor life and reducing incidents of brake pedal pulsation.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: What I remember most was the debate surrounding replacement brake rotors. In the late 1990s, “offshore manufacturers” were selling brake rotors at prices well below fair market value. By 2006, the federal government had begun investigating the situation and imposed antidumping duties on certain imports.
paras.zh: 我记得最多的是围绕更换制动转子的争论。在20世纪90年代末， “离岸制造商”以远低于公平市场价格的价格出售制动转子。到2006年，联邦政府已开始调查这一情况，并对某些进口产品征收反倾销税。

paras.en: Within the aftermarket, some brake brands alleged that these inexpensive rotors were unsafe. Their main argument was that manufacturers were reducing rotor weight by making the friction plates thinner and failing to match the original fin design. I remember several press events that highlighted these design differences. I also remember phone calls from other rotor manufacturers arguing that the practice was acceptable because OE rotors were designed with an “eight-times” safety margin.

The lasting effect of these events were on technicians and repair shops. Replacement brake rotors became so inexpensive that installing new ones often cost less than the labor required to machine the originals. The economics allowed shops to recommend new rotors with increasing frequency, based on the rationale that replacement produced a more reliable, comeback-free brake job.

This replacement mindset even prompted California’s Bureau of Automotive Repair to conduct a sting investigation in 2010 targeting shops that recommended new rotors without first measuring the thickness of the existing ones.

Like it or not, we have been spoiled by inexpensive brake rotors over the past 20 years. Their availability permanently changed how some technicians and shops service brake systems. Today, it is not uncommon for technicians to recommend new rotors regardless of whether the existing rotors remain within specification, based on the economics.

The market, however, is always changing. Vehicle brake systems have improved, and modern friction formulations have extended rotor life through better ceramic transfer-layer developments. OEMs have also increased the size and mass of many brake rotors to improve braking performance, manage heat and control noise.

On the parts side, replacement rotor prices have increased because of higher transportation costs, inflation, tariffs and other market pressures. Rotors have also become more sophisticated, incorporating improved hat and heat-dam designs. Coatings and treatments such as ferritic nitrocarburizing have further increased the price of replacement rotors.

In my opinion, we are approaching another perfect storm. As replacement rotor prices rise and original brake rotors become more durable, the economics of replacement versus machining are beginning to converge on some brake jobs—especially when shops compare labor and parts costs while accounting for the rotor’s discard dimension.

As an industry veteran who survived the rotor wars, I see this as a win-win for repair shops. On the labor side, machining rotors can be a profitable again. On the parts side, selling a higher-value replacement rotor can generate more gross-profit dollars.
It may be time to dust off your micrometers and tune up your brake lathes.

paras.zh: Schrader宣布其OE替换TPMS传感器产品组合的最新扩展，以涵盖较新的车辆应用。该公司宣布了五个新的部件编号：

articles.title: Fuel Costs Push FTR Shippers Conditions Index Down in August
articles.author: Kevin Linger

paras.en: FTR’s August 2026 Shippers Conditions Index fell to -15.4 from -8.1 in July, driven primarily by a renewed surge in fuel costs. Freight rates were also a slightly larger negative for shippers during the month.
paras.zh: FTR的2026年8月托运人状况指数从7月的-8.1降至-15.4 ，主要是由于燃料成本再次飙升。本月运费对托运人的负面影响也略大。

paras.en: “We obviously knew that the SCI would take a big hit due to diesel prices jumping more than 50 cents a gallon on average in August after declining in June and July,” said Avery Vise, vice president of trucking at FTR. “Freight rates and tight capacity remain major challenges for shippers, but at least the pain in those areas is not worsening at the rate it was earlier in the year.”
paras.zh: FTR卡车运输副总裁Avery Vise表示： “我们显然知道，由于柴油价格在6月和7月下跌后， 8月份平均每加仑上涨超过50美分， SCI将受到重创。” “货运费率和运力紧张仍然是托运人面临的主要挑战，但至少这些领域的痛苦并没有像今年早些时候那样恶化。”

paras.en: FTR said the index likely deteriorated further in September after diesel prices reached a record high.
paras.zh: FTR表示，在柴油价格创下历史新高后，该指数可能在9月份进一步恶化。

paras.en: “With fuel costs surging to a record high in September, the market continues to be highly unfavorable for shippers, and any prospects for near-term relief seem speculative,” Vise said. “We expect further stabilization in rates and utilization, but both factors look at least mildly negative for shippers over the forecast horizon.”
paras.zh: Vise表示： “随着9月份燃料成本飙升至创纪录的高位，市场对托运人仍然非常不利，任何近期缓解的前景似乎都是投机性的。” “我们预计费率和利用率将进一步稳定，但在预测期内，这两个因素对托运人来说至少是温和的负面影响。”

articles.title: GCIA Donates Recycled Rides at Golf Fundraiser
articles.author: Jason Stahl

paras.en: A presentation of three National Auto Body Council (NABC) Recycled Rides took place Oct. 12 as part of a golf fundraiser by the Georgia Collision Industry Association (GCIA) in Woodstock, Ga.
paras.zh: 10月12日，乔治亚州碰撞工业协会（ GCIA ）在佐治亚州伍德斯托克举办了一场高尔夫筹款活动，其中包括三场国家汽车机构理事会（ NABC ）回收乘坐活动。

paras.en: The GCIA is a non-profit trade association dedicated to promoting professionalism, safety and consumer awareness within the automotive collision repair sector across Georgia. The organization connects collision repair professionals, vendors, insurers and educational entities to navigate industry evolution, advocate for safe repair processes and elevate standards.
paras.zh: GCIA是一个非营利性行业协会，致力于在佐治亚州的汽车碰撞修理行业内促进专业性、安全性和消费者意识。该组织将碰撞维修专业人员、供应商、保险公司和教育实体联系起来，以引导行业发展，倡导安全的维修流程并提高标准。

paras.en: Prior to the golf event, three Atlanta-area residents each received a vehicle to assist as they work and care for their families, thanks to the NABC Recycled Rides program along with vehicle donors Allstate and repair partners Larry’s Body Shop, Babb’s Body Shop and Ed Voyles Collision Center, who are all members of the GCIA.
paras.zh: 在高尔夫活动之前，三名亚特兰大地区的居民分别收到了一辆车，以协助他们工作和照顾他们的家人，这要归功于NABC回收乘车计划以及车辆捐赠者Allstate和维修合作伙伴Larry's Body Shop ， Babb's Body Shop和Ed Voyles Collision Center ，他们都是GCIA的成员。

paras.en: Juliesha Carter was nominated by the Women’s Resource Center. Carter, is a survivor of domestic violence and a mother of five children, including a newborn. Over the years, her family has faced many challenges while working to rebuild their lives and create a safe, stable future. Despite these difficulties, they continue to move forward with hope and determination. She was commuting more than 50 minutes each way to work every day. Reliable transportation is essential not only for maintaining Carter’s employment but also for getting her children to school, appointments, activities and the many responsibilities that come with raising a large family. The financial strain of maintaining dependable transportation had been a constant challenge. This vehicle from Recycled Rides will provide security, stability and peace of mind during a very important time in Carter’s life, allowing her to focus on building a brighter future for her children.

articles.title: Bumper Removal & ADAS Recalibration
articles.author: Counterman Staff

paras.en: Removing a front bumper cover for repairs or modifications can affect advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS). Cameras, radar and other sensors require precise alignment to function properly.
paras.zh: 拆卸前保险杠盖进行维修或改装可能会影响高级驾驶员辅助系统(ADAS)。摄像头、雷达和其他传感器需要精确对准才能正常工作。

paras.en: Remind customers that bumper removal or replacement may require ADAS recalibration, even during routine radiator, condenser or headlight repairs. Always consult manufacturer procedures to ensure proper operation and safety.
paras.zh: 提醒客户，即使在常规散热器、冷凝器或车头灯维修期间，保险杠的拆卸或更换也可能需要ADAS重新校准。始终咨询制造商程序，以确保正确操作和安全。

paras.en: This video is sponsored by The Pronto Network.
paras.zh: 此视频由The Pronto Network赞助。

articles.title: Lightest known pair of neutron stars proves Einstein right yet again
articles.author: Andrey Feldman

paras.en: Astronomers have discovered the lightest known pair of neutron stars — two ultradense stellar remnants that circle each other every 2 hours, 22 minutes, veering toward an inevitable collision about 82 million years from now. By timing radio pulses from one of the stars, the researchers detected three subtle effects predicted by Albert Einstein's general theory of relativity and found that the theory describes the pair's motion to within about 1% — proving the visionary physicist right yet again.
paras.zh: 天文学家发现了已知最轻的中子星对--两颗超密度恒星残骸，每2小时22分钟环绕一次，在大约8200万年后转向不可避免的碰撞。通过对来自其中一颗恒星的无线电脉冲进行定时，研究人员发现了阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦广义相对论预测的三种微妙效应，并发现该理论描述了这对恒星的运动范围在1%左右，再次证明了这位有远见的物理学家的正确性。

paras.en: The researchers published their findings Sept. 15 in the journal Physical Review Letters.
paras.zh: 研究人员于9月15日在《物理评论快报》杂志上发表了他们的研究结果。

paras.en: Neutron stars are the collapsed cores of massive stars that exploded as supernovas. Each packs more mass than the sun into a ball roughly 12 miles (20 kilometers) in diameter. Some, called pulsars, spin rapidly and sweep beams of radio waves across the sky like cosmic lighthouses. Their rotation is so steady that their pulses work as extraordinarily precise clocks.
paras.zh: 中子星是以超新星形式爆炸的大质量恒星的坍缩核心。每个都将比太阳更多的质量装入一个直径约12英里（ 20公里）的球中。有些被称为脉冲星，快速旋转，像宇宙灯塔一样扫过天空中的无线电波束。它们的旋转是如此稳定，以至于它们的脉冲像非常精确的时钟一样工作。

paras.en: Very few pulsars orbit another neutron star. "There are only 30 such double neutron star systems, and the relativistic effects are very strong if they are in compact orbits," study co-author JinLin Han, an astronomer at the National Astronomical Observatories of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, told Live Science via email.
paras.zh: 很少有脉冲星围绕另一颗中子星运行。“只有30个这样的双中子星系统，如果它们在紧凑的轨道上，相对论效应非常强大，”中国科学院国家天文台的天文学家JinLin Han通过电子邮件告诉Live Science。

paras.en: The first such pair, discovered in 1974 and known as the Hulse-Taylor binary, provided the first evidence for gravitational waves — ripples in space-time predicted by Einstein. Such waves carry energy away from an orbiting pair, so its orbit should gradually shrink, and the Hulse-Taylor orbit shrank at just the rate Einstein's theory predicted.
paras.zh: 1974年发现的第一个这样的对，被称为Hulse-Taylor二进制，为引力波提供了第一个证据—爱因斯坦预测的时空涟漪。这种波将能量从轨道对中带走，因此它的轨道应该逐渐收缩，而Hulse-Taylor轨道则以爱因斯坦理论预测的速度收缩。

paras.en: Later, the "double pulsar," which completes an orbit every 2.45 hours, matched the predicted rate to within about 0.01%. Eventually, this shrinking forces such pairs to merge, unleashing gravitational waves like those the Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory and Virgo interferometer picked up in 2017.
paras.zh: 后来，每2.45小时完成一次轨道的“双脉冲星”与预测的速率相匹配，在0.01%左右。最终，这种收缩迫使这些对合并，释放出像激光干涉仪引力波天文台和处女座干涉仪在2017年拾取的引力波。

paras.en: The new system, designated PSR J1856-0039, lies roughly 4,200 to 6,500 light-years from Earth. In 2020, it turned up in a survey of the Milky Way's disk by China's Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical Radio Telescope (FAST), the world's largest single-dish radio telescope.
paras.zh: 这个新系统被命名为PSR J1856-0039 ，距离地球约4200至6500光年。2020年，世界上最大的单碟射电望远镜中国五百米口径球面射电望远镜（ FAST ）对银河系圆盘进行了调查。

paras.en: Get the world’s most fascinating discoveries delivered straight to your inbox.
paras.zh: 将世界上最迷人的发现直接发送到您的收件箱。

paras.en: "We have discovered about 900 pulsars," Han said of his team's work. "After a few follow-up observations, this one is very extraordinary."
paras.zh: “我们已经发现了大约900颗脉冲星，” Han谈到他的团队的工作时说。“经过几次随访观察，这一次非常不寻常。”

paras.en: The pulsar spins about 43 times per second, and the two stars are separated by roughly twice the distance between Earth and the moon. But the "most attractive feature" is the short orbital period of about 2.36 hours, Han said. "This is the second-shortest one, and it must show stronger relativistic effects than the famous double pulsar and the Hulse-Taylor system."
paras.zh: 脉冲星每秒旋转约43次，两颗恒星之间的距离大约是地球和月球之间距离的两倍。但Han说， “最具吸引力的特征”是大约2.36小时的短轨道周期。“这是第二短的，它必须比著名的双脉冲星和Hulse-Taylor系统表现出更强的相对论效应。”

paras.en: The team observed the pair with FAST 17 times between 2020 and 2025, sometimes long enough to cover a whole orbit. The researchers measured the arrival times of the system's pulses and then fit that data to orbital models that accounted for relativistic effects, like subtle changes to the pulse arrival times at different parts of the stars' orbits.
paras.zh: 研究小组在2020年至2025年期间快速观测了17次，有时长度足以覆盖整个轨道。研究人员测量了系统脉冲的到达时间，然后将这些数据拟合到考虑相对论效应的轨道模型中，例如恒星轨道不同部分的脉冲到达时间的微妙变化。

paras.en: "With so many measurements by FAST, which would be hard to match in accuracy with other telescopes, we got not only the basic parameters of the pulsar and its orbit but also three relativistic effects," Han said.
paras.zh: Han说： “由于FAST的测量如此之多，其精度很难与其他望远镜相匹配，我们不仅得到了脉冲星及其轨道的基本参数，还得到了三个相对论效应。”

paras.en: First, the orbit is shrinking as the stars radiate gravitational waves, drawing them about 9 feet (2.7 meters) closer each year. Second, the oval orbit turns slowly, by 17.6 degrees per year — some 150,000 times faster than the relativistic drift of Mercury's orbit. Third, because both gravity and speed slow time, the pulsar's clock runs at a varying pace along the oval orbit, shifting its pulses by up to about half a millisecond.
paras.zh: 首先，随着恒星辐射引力波，轨道正在缩小，每年将它们拉近约9英尺（ 2.7米）。其次，椭圆形轨道转动缓慢，每年17.6度，比水星轨道的相对论漂移快约15万倍。第三，由于重力和速度都很慢，脉冲星的时钟沿着椭圆轨道以不同的速度运行，使其脉冲移动了大约半毫秒。

paras.en: "From these measurements, we determined the pulsar mass and the companion mass," Han explained. "The total mass is the lowest among all known double neutron star systems." The pulsar weighs about 1.3 times as much as the sun, and its companion is just 1.19 solar masses — one of the lowest-mass neutron stars known. Simulations suggest that supernovas can't forge neutron stars much lighter than that.
paras.zh: “通过这些测量，我们确定了脉冲星质量和伴星质量，” Han解释说。“在所有已知的双中子星系统中，总质量是最低的。“脉冲星的重量大约是太阳的1.3倍，它的伴星只有1.19太阳质量，是已知质量最低的中子星之一。模拟表明，超新星不能锻造比这轻得多的中子星。

paras.en: The stars will merge in about 82 million years. That merger will probably leave behind a heavier neutron star of about 2.26 solar masses, though the remnant could instead collapse into a black hole, the researchers estimate.
paras.zh: 这些恒星将在大约8200万年后合并。研究人员估计，这次合并可能会留下一颗质量约为2.26太阳质量的更重的中子星，尽管残骸可能会坍缩成一个黑洞。

paras.en: Any two of the three effects are enough to calculate both stars' masses. The third then serves as an independent check, because if general relativity is correct, all three must point to the same masses — and they do.
paras.zh: 这三种效应中的任意两种都足以计算两颗恒星的质量。第三个则作为一个独立的检验，因为如果广义相对论是正确的，那么所有三个都必须指向相同的质量—他们确实如此。

paras.en: "We found that general relativity is needed to explain the data, and the consistency is about 1%," Han said. The double pulsar test is more precise, but it drew on 16 years of data, compared with about five for the new pair. "Unfortunately, we could not beat this description of gravity," Han added, referring to physicists' hope of finding cracks in Einstein's theory that might reveal new physics.
paras.zh: Han说： “我们发现需要广义相对论来解释数据，一致性约为1%。”双脉冲星测试更精确，但它利用了16年的数据，而新对的数据约为5年。“不幸的是，我们无法击败这种对引力的描述，”韩补充说，他指的是物理学家希望在爱因斯坦的理论中找到可能揭示新物理学的裂缝。

paras.en: Next, the team hopes to detect "frame dragging," an effect in which a spinning mass twists space-time around it, making nearby orbits wobble. "In the future, we will monitor this pulsar, probably over decades, to detect the frame dragging induced by the neutron star's spin," Han said.
paras.zh: 接下来，研究小组希望能够探测到“帧拖动” ，即旋转的质量在其周围扭曲时空，使附近的轨道摆动。“将来，我们可能会在几十年内监测这颗脉冲星，以检测中子星自旋引起的帧拖曳，”韩说。

paras.en: Measuring the effect would reveal the pulsar's moment of inertia, which depends on how its mass is spread out inside. That would provide "a novel constraint" on how matter behaves at the crushing densities in neutron star cores, Han said — one of the biggest open questions in physics.
paras.zh: 测量这种效应将揭示脉冲星的惯性矩，这取决于它的质量如何在内部扩散。Han说，这将为物质在中子星核心的破碎密度下如何表现提供“新颖的约束” ，这是物理学中最大的开放性问题之一。

paras.en: Yang, Z. L., Han, J. L., Su, W. Q., Wang, P. F., Wang, C., Wang, T., Zhou, D. J., Yan, Y., Xu, J., Jing, W. C., Cai, N. N., Xu, R. X., Wang, H. G., & You, X. P. (2026). Relativistic effects of PSR J1856–0039 double neutron star system in a 2.36-Hour compact orbit. Physical Review Letters, 137(12), 121401. https://doi.org/10.1103/hmjp-htd1
paras.zh: Yang, Z. L., Han, J. L., Su, W. Q., Wang, P. F., Wang, C., Wang, T., Zhou, D. J., Yan, Y., Xu, J., Jing, W. C., Cai, N. N., Xu, R. X., Wang, H. G., & You, X. P. (2026). PSR J1856-0039双中子星系统在2.36小时紧凑轨道上的相对论效应。Physical Review Letters ， 137 （ 12 ） ， 121401。https://doi.org/10.1103/hmjp-htd1

paras.en: Andrey got his B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in elementary particle physics from Novosibirsk State University in Russia, and a Ph.D. in string theory from the Weizmann Institute of Science in Israel. He works as a science writer, specializing in physics, space, and technology. His articles have been published in AdvancedScienceNews, PhysicsWorld, Science, and other outlets.
paras.zh: Andrey在俄罗斯新西伯利亚州立大学获得基本粒子物理学学士和硕士学位，并在以色列魏茨曼科学研究所获得弦理论博士学位。他是一名科学作家，专攻物理、空间和技术。他的文章发表在AdvancedScienceNews、PhysicsWorld、Science和其他媒体上。

articles.title: 'The Russians were the problem in the end': Sailor Matt Rutherford on being intercepted by the FSB while attempting to circumnavigate the Arctic Ocean solo
articles.author: Sascha Pare

paras.en: Sailor Matt Rutherford has dreamed for several years of becoming the first person to circumnavigate the Arctic Ocean solo, nonstop and unassisted. He finally set out from western Greenland on June 25 to achieve this goal, but threatening encounters with Russia's security agency less than two months later forced him to reverse course.
paras.zh: 水手马特·卢瑟福（Matt Rutherford）多年来一直梦想成为第一个独自、不间断且无人协助地环绕北冰洋的人。他最终于 6 月 25 日从格陵兰岛西部出发以实现这一目标，但不到两个月后与俄罗斯安全机构的威胁遭遇迫使他改变了路线。

paras.en: Rutherford is the founder and executive director of the nonprofit environmental organization Ocean Research Project, which gathers and analyzes marine data from a sailboat. His route took him around the southern tip of Greenland, through the Denmark Strait and into the Greenland Sea. From there, he sailed through the Norwegian and Barents seas, and reached Russia's Novaya Zemlya archipelago in mid-August.
paras.zh: 卢瑟福是非营利性环境组织海洋研究项目的创始人兼执行董事，该项目收集和分析帆船上的海洋数据。他的路线带他绕过格陵兰岛的南端，穿过丹麦海峡，进入格陵兰海。从那里，他航行穿越挪威和巴伦支海，并于8月中旬抵达俄罗斯的新地岛群岛。

paras.en: He was planning to continue to Canada and end his journey where it started, but Russian officials halted him in his tracks and ordered him to turn around.
paras.zh: 他原本计划继续前往加拿大，并在原地结束旅程，但俄罗斯官员拦住了他，并命令他掉头。

paras.en: On his way home, Rutherford told Live Science about his adventures and why he wants to complete this loop. In an interview on Sept. 23, he also revealed what he'll do differently on his next attempt to avoid another Russian interception.
paras.zh: 在回家的路上，卢瑟福向《生活科学》讲述了他的冒险经历以及他为什么想完成这个循环。在 9 月 23 日的一次采访中，他还透露了下次尝试时他将采取哪些不同的做法来避免俄罗斯再次拦截。

paras.en: Matt Rutherford is a sailor and the founder of the Ocean Research Project, a nonprofit that conducts marine research from a sailboat. Matt is the first solo sailor to complete a circumnavigation of North and South America nonstop. This achievement in 2011 inspired his new circumnavigation project in the Arctic Ocean.
paras.zh: Matt Rutherford是一名水手，也是海洋研究项目的创始人，这是一个在帆船上进行海洋研究的非营利组织。Matt是第一位完成北美和南美不间断环球航行的单人水手。2011年的这一成就激发了他在北冰洋的新环球航行项目。

paras.en: Sascha Pare: Where are you currently, and what are the conditions like?
paras.zh: Sascha Pare：您现在在哪里，情况如何？

paras.en: Matt Rutherford: I'm about halfway between Greenland and Newfoundland in the Labrador Sea. The conditions aren't too bad; I mean, it's close to a gale, but it's not quite a gale. [Editor's note: A gale is defined as an area of sustained surface winds of 34 to 47 knots (39 to 54 miles per hour).] It's just a little hard to do anything. I've got dishes in the sink that are all wedged in there that I really need to deal with — but I don't feel like it, because you're just getting tossed around. Waves are crashing on the cockpit. Normally, I do video calls under a dodger [a canvas screen on a boat or ship that provides protection from spray], and you can see the ocean in the background… But I'm going to get hit by a wave if I do that.
paras.zh: 马特·卢瑟福：我大约位于格陵兰岛和拉布拉多海纽芬兰岛之间。条件还算不错；我的意思是，它接近大风，但又不完全是大风。 [编者注：大风的定义是持续表面风速为 34 至 47 节（39 至 54 英里/小时）的区域。] 做任何事情都有点困难。我的水槽里有一些盘子都卡在里面，我真的需要处理它们——但我不喜欢这样，因为你只是被扔来扔去。海浪拍击着驾驶舱。通常，我会在躲避器（船上的帆布屏幕，提供防溅保护）下进行视频通话，你可以看到背景中的海洋……但如果我这样做，我就会被海浪击中。

paras.en: SP: You're sailing home to Maryland after a rather perilous expedition. How long have you been at sea for?
paras.zh: SP：在一次相当危险的探险之后，你正乘船返回马里兰州的家。你出海多久了？

paras.en: MR: I left in mid-May, and I've been basically underway for the most part since then. At this time, currently, I've only been at sea for a few days, because I left Greenland a few days ago. The longest stretch I was continuously at sea this year is 59 days, although I was planning on doing longer than that, so that sucked. Essentially, I was attempting to do a nonstop, single-handed circumnavigation of the Arctic. That's where this all sort of came out of. I tried in 2018, but you couldn't get the Russian permits. And the Russians were the problem in the end [this year]. I got defeated by Russian bureaucracy, essentially. And there was some weird stuff going on with the ice up there this year. [Editor's note: Sections of the High Arctic were impassable due to a relatively cold summer and solid ice fields.]
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: SP: What happened with the Russians that forced you to turn back?
paras.zh: SP：俄罗斯人发生了什么事情迫使你返回？

paras.en: MR: The FSB got me. [Editor's note: The Federal Security Service (FSB) is Russia's main security agency and a successor to the Soviet Union's KGB.] They boarded me twice, actually. I've never been boarded in the ocean in my life, and I've been sailing 20 years, all over the place. I got about 1,000 miles [1,600 kilometers] into Russia, roughly. I got into the Northern Sea Route. If you just draw a line due north, I was due north of West China — it was way over there, about halfway around the world in the Arctic. I made it about halfway, because I started in Aasiaat, Greenland.
paras.zh: MR：FSB 抓住了我。 [编者注：联邦安全局（FSB）是俄罗斯的主要安全机构，也是苏联克格勃的继承者。] 事实上，他们登机了我两次。我这辈子从来没有登上过大海，我已经航行了20年，去过很多地方。我大约进入俄罗斯约 1,000 英里（1,600 公里）。我进入了北海航线。如果你只是在正北画一条线，我就在中国西部的正北——那儿很远，大约在地球的一半的北极。我大约完成了一半，因为我是从格陵兰岛的阿西亚特出发的。

paras.en: They boarded me once, and then they turned me around and boarded me again. It's a bit of a strange situation, I guess. Two days after I turned around, the ice that I was waiting to open opened, and I sent them an email — the NSRA, the Northern Sea Route Association in Moscow — and said, "Hey, it's open. Can I pretty please go?" And they just got mad at me, like, "You'll be in violation of your permit; you have to turn around."
paras.zh: 他们登机了我一次，然后又把我转过来，再次登机。我想这有点奇怪。我转身两天后，我等待打开的冰打开了，我给他们发了一封电子邮件——NSRA，莫斯科的北海航线协会——并说，“嘿，它已经打开了。我可以走了吗？”他们只是生我的气，比如，“你将违反你的许可；你必须掉头。”

paras.en: SP: You're planning to try the circumnavigation again next year. Will you do anything differently to make sure you complete it?
paras.zh: SP ：您计划明年再次尝试环球航行。您会做些不同的事情来确保完成它吗？

paras.en: MR: The boat's pretty good to go — which is great, because that's a huge time sink. Ideally, hopefully, if I can get north of [the Norwegian archipelago] Svalbard again like I did this year, then I'm going to stay north of [the Russian archipelago] Franz Josef Land, and I'm going to basically ride the polar ice cap all the way from Svalbard to the Northwest Passage — all the way to Alaska and beyond, essentially.
paras.zh: MR：这艘船很适合航行——这很好，因为这会浪费大量的时间。理想情况下，如果我能像今年一样再次到达[挪威群岛]斯瓦尔巴群岛以北，那么我将留在[俄罗斯群岛]弗朗兹约瑟夫地群岛以北，并且我基本上将沿着极地冰盖从斯瓦尔巴群岛一直到西北航道 - 一直到阿拉斯加以及更远的地方。

paras.en: Because I've learned how the FSB operate, and I know where they're keeping their ships now. Even though I was north of Novaya Zemlya, they still were able to get me. But if I'm over there, north of Frank Josef, they don't go that far, so they won't be able to get me up there. I've figured out a couple of other things that I'm not even going to say, honestly — there are workarounds to get them to [leave me alone]. I'm going to go a little bit quiet.
paras.zh: 因为我了解了 FSB 的运作方式，而且我知道他们现在把船只停放在哪里。尽管我在新地岛北部，他们仍然能够抓住我。但如果我在弗兰克约瑟夫以北的地方，他们不会走那么远，所以他们无法带我去那里。老实说，我已经弄清楚了一些我什至不会说的其他事情 - 有一些解决方法可以让他们[别打扰我]。我要安静一点。

paras.en: The NSRA gives you the permit to do this, but the FSB are the people who patrol it. And the FSB don't like the NSRA. I learned that when they boarded me, because they think that they're the ones who should control the Northern Sea Route, not the NSRA. So there's [a] beef between them; they don't talk. There's a lack of communication, which benefits me. I can lean heavy onto the NSRA side, because they don't have boats; they're not going to board you. And they're the ones you have to check in with every 24 hours in Moscow; you've got to send them an email every 24 hours. So I'll do all of that stuff with those guys, but I think there's some ways I can avoid the FSB even knowing where I am, essentially, while still complying with my permit in the NSRA.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Basically, I've got to do the Northern Sea Route without getting within 12 miles [19 km] of any Russian land, period — even a little island, even a rock that sticks out that's 10 feet by 10 feet [3 by 3 m]. That's going to be real tricky, because there are a lot of little islands down there. But the FSB is mostly on the European side; they have almost no boats over on the east side or the middle. So if you can get past the European side by hugging the coast way the hell north, hopefully I can get past where they patrol, and then I can just shoot on through.
paras.zh: 基本上，我必须在走北海路线时，不能进入任何俄罗斯陆地 12 英里 [19 公里] 范围内，哪怕是一个小岛，甚至是一块 10 英尺 x 10 英尺 [3 x 3 m] 突出的岩石。这真的很棘手，因为那里有很多小岛屿。但金融稳定委员会主要是站在欧洲一边；他们在东边或中部几乎没有船。因此，如果你能沿着北边的海岸穿过欧洲一侧，希望我能穿过他们巡逻的地方，然后我就可以继续射击了。

paras.en: Nobody else in the world does this — nobody else in the Arctic, nobody else anywhere. There's literally no other body of water on Earth where you've got to get permits, and then you've got to get boarded like this. It's only Russia, and only north of Russia. And that's because there's a huge amount of natural gas, they think, buried above Russia. So Russia's trying to claim everything to the North Pole.
paras.zh: 世界上没有其他人这样做——北极没有其他人，任何地方都没有其他人这样做。地球上几乎没有其他水域需要您获得许可，然后您必须像这样登上。只有俄罗斯，而且只有俄罗斯北部。他们认为，这是因为俄罗斯上空埋藏着大量天然气。所以俄罗斯试图夺取北极的一切。

paras.en: Technically, it's international waters, so the U.N. is like, "No, this is not right." And Russia's like, "Whatcha gonna do about it?" It's kind of hard to argue with that — and it's north of Russia, so nobody else is there. They've got free rein, and they've got all the icebreakers and whatever else.
paras.zh: 从技术上讲，这是国际水域，所以联合国会说，“不，这是不对的。”俄罗斯则说：“该怎么办？”很难反驳这一点——而且它位于俄罗斯北部，所以没有其他人在那里。他们拥有自由，他们拥有所有的破冰船和其他任何东西。

paras.en: Everything else is about the same. I need to secure my hot sauce better, because every time I open my cabinet, they fall out all over the place. There's little things like that — quality-of-life things. I'll probably bring some more heated socks — electric socks and electric gloves. I'll try to make better videos — but I'm not a content creator, and I don't want to be an influencer.
paras.zh: 其他一切都差不多。我需要更好地固定我的辣酱，因为每次我打开橱柜，它们都会掉落到处。这样的事情很少—生活质量的事情。我可能会带来更多的加热袜子—电动袜子和电动手套。我会努力制作更好的视频，但我不是内容创作者，也不想成为网红。

paras.en: SP: Can you tell me a bit about your background and what led you to this point?
paras.zh: SP：您能告诉我一些您的背景以及是什么导致您走到这一步吗？

paras.en: MR: I did this whole circumnavigation of the Americas — nonstop, single-handed — back in 2011 where I spent 309 days alone at sea on this little 27-foot (8 meters) boat. When I got back from that big, crazy trip — which I made a documentary about ["Red Dot on the Ocean: The Matt Rutherford Story"] — I created a nonprofit called Ocean Research Project, where, basically, we use sailboats to do research. We focused mostly in 2013 and 2014 on garbage-patch-related microplastics. In 2013, we mapped out the eastern side of the Atlantic garbage patch, because nobody had got to the eastern side of it. I think it was 160,000 pieces per square kilometer, or something like that. And then, we did some stuff in 2014 in the Pacific garbage patch with the University of Tokyo; we did a joint paper with them.
paras.zh: MR：早在 2011 年，我就单人不间断地完成了整个美洲的环球航行，当时我在这艘 27 英尺（8 米）长的小船上独自在海上度过了 309 天。当我从那次疯狂的大旅行回来后——我制作了一部关于[“海洋上的红点：马特卢瑟福的故事”]的纪录片——我创建了一个名为海洋研究项目的非营利组织，基本上，我们使用帆船进行研究。 2013 年和 2014 年，我们主要关注与垃圾带相关的微塑料。 2013年，我们绘制了大西洋垃圾带东侧的地图，因为没有人到达过它的东侧。我认为是每平方公里 160,000 件，或者类似的数字。然后，我们在 2014 年与东京大学一起在太平洋垃圾带做了一些事情；我们与他们联合发表了一篇论文。

paras.en: But mostly what we focus on is Arctic research. Since 2015, we've been heading up to Greenland — sometimes the Northwest Passage also, but primarily Greenland — doing research related to glaciers, for the most part. An ocean-terminating glacier sort of has a river of melted water underneath it, and it creates upwelling, and the upwelling has nutrients. So it mixes nutrients with the ocean and creates this perfect recipe for growth for phytoplankton and zooplankton. And then, we look at the different stages of decay between an ocean-terminating glacier, a land-retreated glacier or a deglaciated fjord. In the middle phase, when a glacier starts retreating back on land, it just creates a river of muddy water, essentially; it turns the fjord into a mud puddle. You can't have photosynthesis if you're in a mud puddle.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: SP: Have you been collecting samples or data on this expedition?
paras.zh: SP：您在这次探险中收集过样本或数据吗？

paras.en: MR: Well, it's a little tricky on a boat under these circumstances. I took 50 samples, which were just water samples, and those were from Newfoundland to Aasiaat, Greenland. Nicole [Nicole Trenholm, Ocean Research Project's science director] has a NASA internship out at JPL [Jet Propulsion Laboratory]. She was publishing a paper looking at their model that they have [ECCO-Darwin], and I've kind of forced my way into the paper — well, the organization did, with Nicole's help — by adding these samples. Now we have in situ data, physical data, that we can compare to the model data. That was the only thing we did this year. It's a couple-thousand-mile stretch with 50 water samples in it, so it's a pretty straightforward sort of thing.
paras.zh: MR：嗯，在这种情况下在船上有点棘手。我采集了50个样本，这些样本只是水样本，这些样本是从纽芬兰到格陵兰岛的阿西亚特。 Nicole [Nicole Trenholm，海洋研究项目的科学总监] 在 NASA 喷气推进实验室 (JPL) 实习。她正在发表一篇论文，研究他们拥有的模型 [ECCO-Darwin]，而我通过添加这些样本，强行进入了这篇论文——好吧，该组织在 Nicole 的帮助下做到了。现在我们有了现场数据、物理数据，我们可以将其与模型数据进行比较。这是我们今年唯一做的事情。这是一段数千英里的路程，包含 50 个水样，所以这是一件非常简单的事情。

paras.en: Nicole is trying to publish multiple peer-reviewed scientific papers from our previous data. She's got a traffic jam of data, so she needed some time to finish publishing papers from stuff we've collected over the last few years. There is no money anyways. I could still grab some samples on the way up there [Greenland]. And it's trying to promote the nonprofit through it, because people will pay a lot more attention to this stuff than they pay to traditional research expeditions.
paras.zh: 妮可正试图根据我们之前的数据发表多篇经过同行评审的科学论文。她的数据很拥堵，所以她需要一些时间来根据我们过去几年收集的资料来完成论文发表。反正也没钱。我仍然可以在前往格陵兰岛的途中获取一些样本。它试图通过它来促进非营利组织的发展，因为人们对这些东西的关注会比对传统研究探险的关注要多得多。

paras.en: - 'If you do want to be a criminal, there is no better place to do it': Author Rose George dives into the dark depths of the fishing industry
paras.zh: - “如果你真的想成为一名罪犯，没有比这更好的地方了” ：作家Rose George深入到渔业的黑暗深处

paras.en: - 'They don't deserve this beauty and this breathtaking fragility': Former Antarctic tour guides told researchers why they quit the troubling industry
paras.zh: - “他们不值得拥有这样的美丽和令人惊叹的脆弱”：前南极导游告诉研究人员他们为何退出这个令人不安的行业

paras.en: - The ozone layer was supposed to be healing. So why is this year's Antarctic ozone hole so big?
paras.zh: - 臭氧层应该正在愈合。那么今年的南极臭氧空洞为何如此之大呢？

paras.en: SP: What are your hopes for the Ocean Research Project once you tick off this goal?
paras.zh: SP ：一旦你完成了这个目标，你对海洋研究项目有什么期望？

paras.en: MR: Basically, we're trying to expand the organization over the next couple of years. I'd like to bring in another one or two more scientists, because we're up there for three months in Greenland, and sometimes we go to the Northwest Passage — and it's a lot for one scientist.
paras.zh: MR：基本上，我们正在努力在未来几年内扩大组织规模。我想再引进一到两名科学家，因为我们在格陵兰岛呆了三个月，有时我们会去西北航道——这对于一名科学家来说是很多。

paras.en: The big problem we're having is that when Elon Musk was part of DOGE [U.S. Department of Government Efficiency], they cut a massive amount of polar funding — something like 88% of it — because apparently climate change is a hoax and they hate it and you're not allowed to research it either, right?
paras.zh: 我们面临的最大问题是，当伊隆·马斯克（ Elon Musk ）是DOGE （美国政府效率部）的一员时，他们削减了大量的极地资金—大约88 ％ —因为显然气候变化是一个骗局，他们讨厌它，你也不允许研究它，对吧？

paras.en: Basically, nobody's got money. We don't typically get NSF [National Science Foundation] funding; we get more foundation funding, because it's hard to get NSF funding, even before all this stuff. Now that the funding has been cut on the governmental level, a lot more scientists are going after the foundation grants that we used to have a lot less competition for. That makes it a little tricky, too, because now they're getting a flood of requests that they didn't usually get in the past.
paras.zh: 基本上，没有人有钱。我们通常不会获得NSF （国家科学基金会）的资助；我们会获得更多的基金会资金，因为即使在所有这些东西之前，也很难获得NSF的资助。现在，政府层面的资金已经削减，越来越多的科学家正在追求我们曾经竞争激烈的基金会拨款。这也有点棘手，因为现在他们收到了大量过去通常不会收到的请求。

paras.en: This interview has been condensed and edited lightly for clarity.
paras.zh: 为清楚起见，对采访进行了压缩和编辑。

paras.zh: 帮助我们改进Live Science Pro ：我们一直在努力改进我们的内容。请在此处提供有关专业版的反馈。

paras.en: Sascha is a U.K.-based staff writer at Live Science. She holds a bachelor’s degree in biology from the University of Southampton in England and a master’s degree in science communication from Imperial College London. Her work has appeared in The Guardian and the health website Zoe. Besides writing, she enjoys playing tennis, bread-making and browsing second-hand shops for hidden gems.
paras.zh: Sascha是Live Science的英国特约撰稿人。她拥有英国南安普敦大学的生物学学士学位和伦敦帝国理工学院的科学传播硕士学位。她的作品出现在《卫报》和健康网站Zoe上。除了写作，她还喜欢打网球、做面包和浏览二手商店寻找隐藏的宝石。

articles.title: Uranium from World War II reveals how close the Nazis were to an atomic bomb
articles.author: Tom Metcalfe

paras.en: The Nazis were far from completing a working reactor for their atomic bomb program, despite claims by the project's leader that it was almost ready, a new study finds.
paras.zh: 一项新的研究发现，纳粹远未完成其原子弹计划的反应堆，尽管该项目的负责人声称它已几乎准备就绪。

paras.en: The German physicist Werner Heisenberg wrote in 1947 that the reactor for the "Nazi bomb" project — which culminated in Germany's B8 nuclear reactor — was almost finished at the end of World War II.
paras.zh: 德国物理学家维尔纳·海森堡 (Werner Heisenberg) 在 1947 年写道，“纳粹炸弹”项目的反应堆（最终形成了德国的 B8 核反应堆）在二战末期几乎完工。

paras.en: Heisenberg, who led the reactor's development, claimed the reactor was "just insufficient" to create a self-sustaining fission reaction and that it lacked only a "relatively small amount of uranium" to work.
paras.zh: 领导该反应堆开发的海森堡声称，该反应堆“不足以”产生自持裂变反应，而且它只缺乏“相对少量的铀”来发挥作用。

paras.en: If it had worked, the B8 reactor would have confirmed that a fission chain reaction was possible, marking a key step toward the German development of an atomic bomb. It could have also spurred the development of specialized fission reactors used to create weapons-grade plutonium from uranium. Instead, the atomic bomb was developed first by the United States and was used to force the surrender of Japan in August 1945. (Germany had already surrendered in May 1945.)
paras.zh: 如果成功的话，B8 反应堆将证实裂变链式反应是可能的，这标志着德国研制原子弹的关键一步。它还可能刺激用于从铀制造武器级钚的专用裂变反应堆的发展。相反，原子弹是由美国首先研制出来的，并于 1945 年 8 月用来迫使日本投降。（德国已于 1945 年 5 月投降。）

paras.en: The new study, published Sept. 29 in the journal PNAS Nexus, used historical documents and forensic investigations of two of the project's surviving uranium cubes to refute Heisenberg's claim. The new research indicates that the German B8 reactor had less than half the amount of "heavy water" and about half the amount of uranium it would have needed for a continuous chain reaction.
paras.zh: 这项新研究于 9 月 29 日发表在《PNAS Nexus》杂志上，利用历史文献和对该项目中幸存的两个铀立方体的法医调查来反驳海森堡的说法。新的研究表明，德国 B8 反应堆的“重水”量不到连续链式反应所需量的一半，铀量也只有其一半左右。

paras.en: "My results argue that Heisenberg was off by roughly a factor of two," said first author Patrick Park, a doctoral student at Princeton University who co-wrote the study while at Columbia University.
paras.zh: “我的研究结果表明，海森堡的误差大约是两倍，”第一作者帕特里克·帕克（Patrick Park）说，他是普林斯顿大学的博士生，在哥伦比亚大学期间与人共同撰写了这项研究。

paras.en: Park said Heisenberg's mistake was understandable: His calculations were only approximate, and the project was relocated to a rock cellar in the town of Haigerloch, Germany, after Berlin was bombed.
paras.zh: 帕克表示，海森堡的错误是可以理解的：他的计算只是近似值，柏林遭到轰炸后，该项目被转移到德国海格洛赫镇的一个岩石地窖。

paras.en: Get the world’s most fascinating discoveries delivered straight to your inbox.
paras.zh: 将世界上最迷人的发现直接发送到您的收件箱。

paras.en: "People were dying or starving and so these reactor calculations were not his first priority," while many details of neutron physics were unknown at that time, Park told Live Science in an email. "Given these circumstances, I think he did the best he could."
paras.zh: 帕克在一封电子邮件中告诉《生活科学》，“人们正在死去或挨饿，因此这些反应堆计算不是他的首要任务”，而当时中子物理学的许多细节尚不清楚。 “考虑到这些情况，我认为他已经尽力了。”

paras.en: To answer the question of how far the reactor for the Nazi bomb project got, the scientists began by tracing archival records of hundreds of uranium cubes that had been used by German scientists. The B8 reactor consisted of five concentric circles of uranium cubes suspended on chains within the heavy water tank. The German scientists planned to place a radium-beryllium neutron source into the reactor's core to kick-start the chain reaction with a flood of neutrons that would split the uranium nuclei and release more neutrons, furthering the chain reaction.
paras.zh: 为了回答纳粹炸弹项目的反应堆进展到何种程度的问题，科学家们首先追踪了德国科学家使用过的数百个铀立方体的档案记录。 B8 反应堆由五个同心圆铀立方体组成，悬挂在重水箱内的链条上。德国科学家计划在反应堆堆芯中放置一个镭铍中子源，用大量中子启动链式反应，这些中子会分裂铀核并释放更多中子，从而进一步促进链式反应。

paras.en: Heavy water is a form of water that contains the neutron-heavy hydrogen isotope deuterium. Like the mainly-graphite blocks and rods used in many reactors, it can be used to "moderate" or slow down fast neutrons created in a fission reaction so they trigger fission — and more neutrons — in nearby uranium atoms. The Germans also used small amounts of graphite in their reactor, but as a coating to reflect neutrons back into the chamber.
paras.zh: 重水是一种含有中子重氢同位素氘的水。就像许多反应堆中使用的主要是石墨块和棒一样，它可以用来“慢化”或减慢裂变反应中产生的快中子，以便它们在附近的铀原子中引发裂变 - 以及更多的中子。德国人还在他们的反应堆中使用了少量石墨，但作为将中子反射回反应室的涂层。

paras.en: By combining the records of the cubes, heavy water and graphite used by the German scientists with measurements of the two surviving cubes, the study authors created a mathematical model of the reactor that agreed closely with historical measurements. This enabled them to establish that the heavy water reactor was far from achieving a stable reaction. The findings also helped them examine the suggestion that the Germans should have instead built a graphite-based reactor like the nuclear pile developed at the University of Chicago to build the American bomb.
paras.zh: 通过将德国科学家使用的立方体、重水和石墨的记录与两个幸存立方体的测量相结合，研究作者创建了一个与历史测量结果非常吻合的反应堆数学模型。这使他们能够确定重水反应堆远未实现稳定的反应。这些发现还帮助他们检验了德国人应该建造石墨基反应堆的建议，就像芝加哥大学开发的核堆来制造美国炸弹。

paras.en: But the study authors determined that a graphite-moderated reactor was unfeasible in wartime Germany because the local supply of coal available to create graphite contained high levels of neutron-absorbing boron, making it useless.
paras.zh: 但研究作者确定，石墨慢化反应堆在战时德国是不可行的，因为当地供应的可用于制造石墨的煤炭含有高含量的中子吸收硼，使其毫无用处。

paras.en: Instead, the heavy water used in the B8 reactor was produced at a single factory in Norway, which was occupied by Germany from April 1940 until May 1945. However, the reactor contained only about 370 gallons (1,400 liters) of heavy water, instead of the more than 780 gallons (roughly 3,000 liters) it would have needed, the researchers determined.
paras.zh: 相反，B8 反应堆中使用的重水是在挪威的一家工厂生产的，该工厂从 1940 年 4 月到 1945 年 5 月一直被德国占领。然而，研究人员确定，该反应堆仅含有约 370 加仑（1,400 升）重水，而不是其所需的超过 780 加仑（约 3,000 升）重水。

paras.en: Heavy water makes up a tiny fraction of a percent of ordinary water, and extracting it by electrolysis in the Norwegian factory took extraordinary effort. The factory was producing as much heavy water as it could, but the B8 reactor would have needed more than twice the amount it produced during the entire war, the researchers wrote.
paras.zh: 重水仅占普通水的百分之一，在挪威工厂通过电解提取重水需要付出巨大的努力。研究人员写道，该工厂正在尽可能多地生产重水，但 B8 反应堆所需的重水量是整个战争期间生产量的两倍多。

paras.en: Another finding is that the B8 reactor had about half the amount of uranium it would have needed to sustain a fission chain reaction. The reactor contained a total of 664 cubes, each weighing about 5.11 pounds (2.32 kilograms), for a total of 3,390 pounds (1,540 kilograms) of uranium. Similar cubes were distributed among other experimental groups, giving a total inventory in wartime Germany of about 1,100 cubes of uranium.
paras.zh: 另一个发现是，B8 反应堆的铀含量约为维持裂变链式反应所需的一半。该反应堆总共包含 664 个立方体，每个立方体重约 5.11 磅（2.32 千克），总计 3,390 磅（1,540 千克）铀。类似的立方体被分发到其他实验组中，战时德国的铀库存总量约为 1,100 立方体。

paras.en: But the researchers determined that the B8 reactor would have needed at least 1,200 cubes to work. Germany, therefore, was not about to develop a reactor for an atomic bomb in 1945. Contrary to Heisenberg's claims, the heavy-water reactor was not nearly ready, and a working graphite reactor was impossible.
paras.zh: 但研究人员确定 B8 反应堆至少需要 1,200 个立方体才能工作。因此，德国在 1945 年并不打算开发用于原子弹的反应堆。与海森堡的说法相反，重水反应堆还没有完全准备好，而且石墨反应堆也不可能投入使用。

paras.en: "We conclude Germany could not have built heavy water nor graphite reactors during World War II," the researchers wrote.
paras.zh: 研究人员写道：“我们的结论是，德国在二战期间不可能建造重水反应堆或石墨反应堆。”

paras.en: Mark Walker, a historian at Union College in Schenectady, New York, who wasn't involved in the study, said the findings explain Germany's decision to develop a heavy-water reactor, since a graphite reactor was not feasible and they didn't know at the time how much heavy water would be needed.
paras.zh: 纽约斯克内克塔迪联合学院的历史学家马克·沃克（ Mark Walker ）没有参与这项研究，他说，研究结果解释了德国发展重水反应堆的决定，因为石墨反应堆不可行，他们当时不知道需要多少重水。

paras.en: Walker is the author of "Hitler's Atomic Bomb: History, Legend, and the Twin Legacies of Auschwitz and Hiroshima" (Cambridge University Press, 2024) and a noted expert on Germany's wartime nuclear efforts. He agreed that Germany could not have made a graphite reactor during World War II.
paras.zh: 沃克是《希特勒的原子弹：历史、传说以及奥斯威辛和广岛的双重遗产》（剑桥大学出版社，2024 年）一书的作者，也是德国战时核努力的著名专家。他同意德国在二战期间不可能制造出石墨反应堆。

paras.en: "This paper argues that if the Germans had done something they did not do, then this would have failed," he told Live Science in an email. "While this is counterfactual history, it is an interesting engineering analysis."
paras.zh: “这篇论文认为，如果德国人做了他们没有做的事情，那么这件事就会失败，”他在一封电子邮件中告诉《生活科学》。 “虽然这是反事实的历史，但这是一个有趣的工程分析。”

paras.en: Park, P. J., Robertson, B., Hiebert, M. E., Zhao, J., Sivels, C. B., & Koeth, T. W. (2026). Nuclear archaeology reassesses Heisenberg’s last reactor experiment. PNAS Nexus, 5(9). https://doi.org/10.1093/pnasnexus/pgag282
paras.zh: Park, P. J., Robertson, B., Hiebert, M. E., Zhao, J., Sivels, C.B., & Koeth, T. W. (2026).核考古学重新评估了海森堡的最后一个反应堆实验。PNAS Nexus ， 5 （ 9 ）。https://doi.org/10.1093/pnasnexus/pgag282

paras.en: Tom Metcalfe is a freelance journalist and regular Live Science contributor who is based in London in the United Kingdom. Tom writes mainly about science, space, archaeology, the Earth and the oceans. He has also written for the BBC, NBC News, National Geographic, Scientific American, Air & Space, and many others.
paras.zh: 汤姆·梅特卡夫 (Tom Metcalfe) 是一名自由撰稿人，也是《Live Science》的定期撰稿人，常驻英国伦敦。汤姆主要撰写有关科学、太空、考古学、地球和海洋的文章。他还为 BBC、NBC 新闻、国家地理、科学美国人、航空航天等多家媒体撰稿。

articles.title: See the Scientific and the Mundane Become Surprisingly Dazzling When Viewed Through a Microscope, From Neurons to Ballpoint Pens

paras.en: The winning images have been announced for the 52nd Nikon Small World Photomicrography Competition. This year’s winners—all captured through a microscope—include zoomed-in shots of slime mold spores, baby sea urchins bathed in fluorescence and everyday writing utensils transformed into enchanted objects.
paras.zh: 第 52 届尼康小世界显微摄影大赛的获奖照片已公布。今年的获奖者——全部都是通过显微镜捕捉到的——包括粘菌孢子的放大照片、沐浴在荧光中的小海胆以及变成魔法物体的日常书写用具。

paras.en: From a pool of more than 1,800 entries submitted from 69 countries, the judges selected 20 winners as well as honorable mentions and images of distinction. Ole Bielfeldt, a student and experimental photographer in Cologne, Germany, clinched first place with his otherworldly shot of a printer in motion—a project he started two years ago.
paras.zh: 评委们从来自 69 个国家/地区提交的 1,800 多份参赛作品中选出了 20 名获奖者以及荣誉奖和杰出图像。德国科隆的学生兼实验摄影师奥勒·比尔费尔特 (Ole Bielfeldt) 以其超凡脱俗的运转中的打印机照片夺得第一名，这是他两年前启动的一个项目。

paras.en: “The beautiful thing about microscopy is that it lets us discover the incredible invisible worlds around us,” Quinten Geldhof, a technical designer at Boston’s Museum of Science and one of this year’s judges, tells Smithsonian magazine in an email. “Getting to see an appliance that we use in our day to day lives, portrayed with such incredible detail, really made this image stand out.”
paras.zh: “显微镜的美妙之处在于，它让我们发现周围令人难以置信的看不见的世界，”波士顿科学博物馆的技术设计师、今年的评委之一昆腾·格尔德霍夫 (Quinten Geldhof) 在一封电子邮件中告诉《史密森尼》杂志。 “看到我们在日常生活中使用的电器，以如此令人难以置信的细节描绘，确实使这张图像脱颖而出。”

paras.en: In Bielfeldt’s winning image, globs of ink stretch down through a fog of flash, dripping onto a slice of white paper. If you tilt your head slightly, nascent letters start to appear: m-a-c. In full, Bielfeldt was spelling “macrofying,” which is the name of his Instagram account boasting more than one million followers.
paras.zh: 在比尔费尔特的获奖图像中，墨滴穿过闪光的雾气向下延伸，滴到一张白纸上。如果您稍微倾斜头部，新生字母就会开始出现：m-a-c。比尔费尔特的完整拼写是“macrofying”，这是他拥有超过 100 万粉丝的 Instagram 帐户的名称。

paras.en: “I’ve kind of built a bit of respect for the printer,” he says to Smithsonian. “It’s such a crazy thing that just moves super fast while simultaneously shooting out these little droplets.”
paras.zh: “我对打印机有点尊重，”他对史密森尼说。 “这是一件非常疯狂的事情，它移动速度超快，同时射出这些小水滴。”

paras.en: To effectively photograph the printing process, Bielfeldt had to “reverse-engineer” the printer, he says, setting the printhead still and instead shifting the paper beneath it. He then captured the ink-injecting process using flash and his own custom-built equipment.
paras.zh: 他说，为了有效地拍摄打印过程，比尔费尔特必须对打印机进行“逆向工程”，将打印头设置为静止，而不是移动打印头下方的纸张。然后，他使用闪光灯和自己定制的设备拍摄了墨水注入过程。

paras.en: Bielfeldt, who enjoys turning his lens on seemingly mundane objects, says he was surprised at the messiness of the ink nozzles when he got his first up-close glimpse. “It’s almost like in nature, very all over the place, while still following kind of a structure,” he says.
paras.zh: 比尔费尔特喜欢将镜头转向看似平凡的物体，他说，当他第一次近距离观察墨水喷嘴时，他对墨水喷嘴的混乱感到惊讶。 “这几乎就像自然界一样，无处不在，同时仍然遵循某种结构，”他说。

paras.en: The 4th place winner, Justin Theodore Benttinen, also took a surreal look at a ubiquitous object. The photographer from Berkeley, California, snapped the shimmering tip of a ballpoint pen, magnified 20 times.
paras.zh: 第四名获得者贾斯汀·西奥多·本蒂宁（Justin Theodore Benttinen）也以超现实的视角观察了一个无处不在的物体。这位来自加利福尼亚州伯克利的摄影师拍摄了放大 20 倍的圆珠笔闪闪发光的笔尖。

paras.en: “One of the core principles of my photographic practice is to find the repetition of patterns throughout both the built and natural worlds at different scales,” Benttinen says in an email. “In a more flippant tone,” he adds, “I just thought it looked cool.”
paras.zh: “我摄影实践的核心原则之一是在不同尺度的建筑世界和自然世界中找到图案的重复，”本蒂宁在一封电子邮件中说道。 “用一种更轻率的语气，”他补充道，“我只是觉得它看起来很酷。”

paras.en: Other photographers captured biological phenomena, such as the 11th-place winner, Svenja Carolin Kling, a marine biology PhD student at the Scripps Institution of Oceanography in California. Kling imaged a 20-day-old sea urchin larva, glittering with blue fluorescence.
paras.zh: 其他摄影师也捕捉到了生物现象，例如第 11 名获奖者 Svenja Carolin Kling，她是加州斯克里普斯海洋学研究所的海洋生物学博士生。克林拍摄了一只 20 天大的海胆幼虫，它闪烁着蓝色荧光。

paras.en: “My research is on genetic tools in sea urchins because they are a model organism for developmental biology research,” Kling says in an email. “I basically ‘made’ this urchin myself.”
paras.zh: “我的研究是海胆的遗传工具，因为它们是发育生物学研究的模式生物，”克林在一封电子邮件中说。 “这个顽童基本上是我自己‘制作’的。”

paras.en: A month ago, the winners of the video version of Nikon’s contest, called Small World in Motion, were unveiled. But several weeks later, the winner, Ning Xu of the National University of Singapore, was stripped of first place, after an investigation found he had not followed proper protocols regarding generative artificial intelligence. (In a now-deleted LinkedIn post, Xu said that A.I. was used in post-production to enhance certain features, but not to generate the film, reported Nature’s Rachel Fieldhouse in September.)
paras.zh: 一个月前，尼康竞赛视频版“运动中的小世界”揭晓了获奖者名单。但几周后，获胜者、新加坡国立大学的徐宁被剥夺了第一名的位置，因为调查发现他没有遵循有关生成人工智能的正确协议。 （据《自然》杂志的 Rachel Fieldhouse 9 月报道，徐在 LinkedIn 的一篇现已删除的帖子中表示，人工智能用于后期制作是为了增强某些功能，但不是为了生成电影。）

paras.en: In a statement earlier this month, Nikon addressed the change to the rankings in its video contest. “This decision is based solely on the submitted video’s eligibility under the rules outlined for this competition. It should not be interpreted as a judgment of the entrant’s professional reputation, scientific contributions or intent,” per the statement. “Advances in imaging and artificial intelligence continue to evolve rapidly, creating new challenges for organizations across many fields.”
paras.zh: 在本月早些时候的一份声明中，尼康谈到了视频竞赛排名的变化。声明称：“这一决定仅基于提交的视频在本次竞赛规则下的资格。它不应被解释为对参赛者的专业声誉、科学贡献或意图的判断。” “成像和人工智能的进步继续快速发展，为许多领域的组织带来了新的挑战。”

paras.en: Bielfeldt says he doesn’t mind the use of A.I. when properly disclosed. But he’d rather it not touch his art. In the case of the printer, with its internal chaos, he doubts that generative A.I. would have reproduced it accurately. “For me, it’s a great tool to do stuff that I don’t want to do,” he says, “but I want to keep it away from the stuff that I have fun doing.”
paras.zh: 比尔费尔特说他不介意使用人工智能。当正确披露时。但他宁愿它不要触及他的艺术。就打印机而言，由于其内部混乱，他对生成式人工智能的能力表示怀疑。会准确地再现它。 “对我来说，这是一个很棒的工具，可以做我不想做的事情，”他说，“但我想让它远离我喜欢做的事情。”

paras.en: All the recognized images can be found in a gallery on the Nikon Small World website. You can see the rest of the second- through tenth-place winners below.
paras.zh: 所有已识别的图像都可以在尼康小世界网站上的图库中找到。您可以在下面看到其余的第二名到第十名获奖者。

articles.title: These Snakes Can Cartwheel Away From Danger. Scientists Just Uncovered How the Slithering Creatures Perform Their Acrobatic Rolls

paras.en: Dwarf reed snakes spend much of their time hiding under rocks, logs or leaf litter, trying to avoid being eaten. But when these small, slithering creatures feel threatened, they’ve perfected a unique method of fleeing from danger: cartwheeling.
paras.zh: 矮芦苇蛇大部分时间都躲在岩石、原木或落叶下，试图避免被吃掉。但当这些滑行的小生物感到受到威胁时，它们会完善一种独特的逃离危险的方法：侧手翻。

paras.en: Scientists first described this roly-poly behavior several years ago, based on observations of a snake spotted wheeling itself down a road in northwest Malaysia. Now, a different team of researchers says they have figured out how these diminutive snakes pull off the acrobatic feat. Their findings were described in a study published on October 19 in the journal Current Biology.
paras.zh: 几年前，科学家们根据对马来西亚西北部道路上发现的一条蛇的观察，首次描述了这种不倒翁行为。现在，另一个研究小组表示，他们已经弄清楚了这些小蛇是如何完成这项杂技壮举的。 10 月 19 日发表在《当代生物学》杂志上的一项研究描述了他们的发现。

paras.en: Dwarf reed snakes (Pseudorabdion longiceps) are short, slender, nocturnal snakes that live in Southeast Asia. They grow to a maximum length of nine inches. Despite their petite stature and penchant for hiding, they’re still vulnerable to predation from birds and other snakes, including the striped coral snake.
paras.zh: 矮芦苇蛇（Pseudorabdion longiceps）是生活在东南亚的短而细长的夜行性蛇。它们的最大长度可达九英寸。尽管它们身材娇小并且喜欢躲藏，但它们仍然容易受到鸟类和其他蛇（包括条纹珊瑚蛇）的捕食。

paras.en: Researchers had heard anecdotal tales of dwarf reed snakes cartwheeling away from danger. In August 2019, they finally caught the unusual behavior on camera. A group of scientists was conducting surveys for other species when they stumbled upon a dwarf reed snake crossing a road. They apparently startled the creature, because it curled its body into a coil and began rolling downhill away from them.
paras.zh: 研究人员听说过矮芦苇蛇翻滚躲避危险的轶事。 2019年8月，他们终于用镜头捕捉到了这一异常行为。一群科学家正在对其他物种进行调查时，偶然发现了一条穿过马路的矮芦苇蛇。他们显然吓到了这个生物，因为它把身体卷成一圈，开始滚下山坡远离他们。

paras.en: Intrigued, the researchers carefully caught the snake, placed it on a flat area and brought out a camera. Once again, the snake rolled away—this time without the help of gravity. Scientists described that encounter in the journal Biotropica in 2023, marking the first time cartwheeling had been formally observed in any snake or reptile more broadly.
paras.zh: 出于好奇，研究人员小心地抓住了这条蛇，将其放在平坦的地方，并拿出了相机。蛇再次滚走了——这次没有重力的帮助。科学家于 2023 年在《Biotropica》杂志上描述了这次遭遇，这标志着首次在任何蛇或爬行动物中正式观察到侧手翻。

paras.en: Ecologist Yosuke Kojima of Toho University in Japan heard about this strange behavior seven years ago from a colleague in Malaysia, reports Science News’ Maria Temming. And after seeing it for himself, Kojima was “amazed by the dynamic movement and immediately wanted to learn more about it,” he tells Defector’s Sabrina Imbler.
paras.zh: 据《科学新闻》的玛丽亚·特明报道，日本东邦大学的生态学家小岛洋介七年前从马来西亚的一位同事那里听说了这种奇怪的行为。在亲眼目睹了它之后，小岛“对这个充满活力的运动感到惊讶，并立即想了解更多信息”，他告诉《叛逃者》的萨布丽娜·伊布勒(Sabrina Imbler)。

paras.en: So, Kojima and colleagues went to Malaysia’s Kubah National Park and gathered several snakes belonging to the Pseudorabdion genus: one P. longiceps, one P. collaris and 11 P. saravacense. They also wrangled six reed snakes of the Calamaria genus for comparison.
paras.zh: 因此，小岛和同事前往马来西亚的库巴国家公园，收集了几条属于拟蛇属的蛇：一条 P. longiceps、一条 P. colonis 和 11 条 P. saravacense。他们还对六条鱿鱼属的芦苇蛇进行了比较。

paras.en: The researchers brought the slithering creatures back to their laboratory, where they had constructed a snake-size racetrack equipped with cameras. One at a time, they placed the snakes at one end of the track, then gently tapped them to see if they would roll.
paras.zh: 研究人员将这些滑行的生物带回实验室，在那里他们建造了一个配备了摄像头的蛇大小的跑道。他们一次一根地把蛇放在轨道的一端，然后轻轻地敲击它们，看看它们是否会滚动。

paras.en: None of the Calamaria reed snakes cartwheeled—they simply slithered down the track like normal. But all 13 members of the Pseudorabdion genus exhibited the rolling locomotion, reaching top speeds of 3.8 to 8.3 miles per hour.
paras.zh: 鱿鱼芦苇蛇都没有侧翻——它们只是像平常一样沿着轨道滑行。但 Pseudorabdion 属的所有 13 个成员都表现出滚动运动，最高速度可达每小时 3.8 至 8.3 英里。

paras.en: When the researchers analyzed the footage, they were able to see exactly how the Pseudorabdion snakes performed their dexterous dance moves. After breaking down the biomechanics, Kojima was “even more amazed by how complex the movement actually was,” he tells the Defector.
paras.zh: 当研究人员分析这段视频时，他们能够准确地看到伪蛇是如何表演灵巧的舞蹈动作的。在分解了生物力学之后，小岛“对这个运动实际上的复杂程度感到更加惊讶”，他告诉叛逃者。

paras.en: A snake starts by curling its body into a tight curve, with its head lifted off the ground facing the direction of travel. As the snake rolls along the ground like a wheel, its body begins to straighten out and the point where it touches the ground shifts toward its tail. The animal then pushes off the ground with its tail, launching itself into the air. While briefly airborne, the creature twists into an S-shape, forming an arch above its head. It then swings this arch forward and down past one side of its head until that side of its body hits the ground. That contact starts the next cartwheel, allowing the snake to keep rolling forward while alternating which side of its body strikes the ground.
paras.zh: 蛇首先将身体卷成一条紧密的曲线，头离开地面，面向行进的方向。当蛇像轮子一样沿着地面滚动时，它的身体开始伸直，接触地面的点向尾巴方向移动。然后，动物用尾巴将自己推离地面，飞向空中。在短暂的空中飞行时，该生物会扭曲成 S 形，在头顶上方形成一个拱形。然后，它向前和向下摆动这个拱门，经过其头部的一侧，直到其身体的一侧撞到地面。这种接触启动了下一个侧手翻，让蛇继续向前滚动，同时交替用身体的哪一侧接触地面。

paras.en: Through all this precisely coordinated choreography, the snakes hold their heads fairly steady, which the researchers think helps the reptiles keep their bearings.
paras.zh: 通过所有这些精确协调的编排，蛇可以相当稳定地保持头部，研究人员认为这有助于爬行动物保持方向。

paras.en: The Moroccan flic-flac spider is considered the fastest spider in the world. It can reach speeds of up to 3.8 miles per hour to escape danger—and it does that by rolling. However, the tactic eats up a lot of energy, so the spiders can only do it in short bursts.
paras.zh: 摩洛哥弗利弗拉克蜘蛛被认为是世界上跑得最快的蜘蛛。它可以达到每小时 3.8 英里的速度来逃离危险——而且它是通过滚动来实现的。不过，这种战术会消耗大量的能量，所以蜘蛛只能短时间爆发。

paras.en: Scientists now know more about how the snakes execute their cartwheels, but they still don’t fully understand why they move this way. Rolling helps them move quickly—about four times faster than slithering—so it’s undoubtedly useful for evading predators. But it’s likely also an energy-intensive process, and the researchers aren’t sure how long the snakes could keep up their cartwheeling.
paras.zh: 科学家们现在对蛇如何进行侧手翻有了更多的了解，但他们仍然不完全明白它们为什么会这样移动。滚动可以帮助它们快速移动——大约是滑行速度的四倍——所以这对于躲避掠食者来说无疑是有用的。但这也可能是一个能源密集型过程，研究人员不确定蛇能保持侧手翻多久。

paras.en: Many questions remain unanswered, including how the snakes evolved such a “strange and possibly demanding” movement, Jessica Tingle, a biologist at Brown University who was not involved in the study, tells Science News. And do dwarf reed snakes have “something special in their anatomy, physiology or neural control that lets them do it when their close relatives apparently can’t or don’t?”
paras.zh: 布朗大学生物学家杰西卡·廷格尔（未参与这项研究）告诉《科学新闻》，许多问题仍未得到解答，包括蛇是如何进化出这种“奇怪且可能要求很高”的运动的。矮芦苇蛇是否“在解剖学、生理学或神经控制方面有一些特殊的东西，可以让它们在它们的近亲显然不能或不做的时候做到这一点？”

paras.en: The new work also opens the possibility of every snake secretly having the traits to roll away, Tingle notes. “Do all snakes have the basic equipment, and they just don’t use it?”
paras.zh: 廷格尔指出，这项新研究还开启了每条蛇都秘密拥有滚走特征的可能性。 “是不是所有的蛇都有基本的装备，只是他们不使用？”

articles.title: She Painted the First Known Self-Portrait of an Artist at Work—and Signed It—Nearly 500 Years Ago. Who Was Catharina van Hemessen?

paras.en: When Catharina van Hemessen was 20, she painted what is widely believed to be the earliest known self-portrait of an artist at work.
paras.zh: Catharina van Hemessen 20 岁时画了一幅被广泛认为是已知最早的艺术家工作自画像。

paras.en: In the 1548 scene, van Hemessen dons a black gown with red velvet sleeves and a modest hair covering. Instead of meeting the viewer’s gaze directly, she looks beyond them, her attention momentarily pulled away from the unfinished painting on her easel. A Latin inscription at the top left of the panel proudly proclaims the artist’s authorship, declaring that “I, Catharina van Hemessen, painted myself.”
